The user-global instruction scope has two ordered roots: `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md` first, then `<agentsHome>/AGENTS.md`. The instruction loader resolves the harness home from `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh`, and `agentsHome` from `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME` or `~/.agents`. `resolveAgentsHome` and `agentsHomeDisplay` in `dsh-home-paths` own that resolution for both `dsh-agent-instructions` and `dsh-skill-filesystem`, so the shared root has one resolver whose tilde expansion and blank-environment handling match the harness home.

The two files are candidates of one candidate group. They deduplicate by trimmed content, so identical copies render once from the harness home, and an unobservable candidate preserves the group's last-good state. A duplicate of budget-retained content keeps being reconciled, so deleting or changing the retained candidate promotes it; a byte-budget omission leaves that candidate and its content duplicates unprobed. The harness-home file keeps the `user-global` scope key that earlier sessions recorded; the shared file carries `agents-global`, and reconciliation probes both roots on resume, so an external edit, a removal, or a newly created file appears as a change notice instead ...
attrs.problem: DSH loads one user-global instruction file, `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`. People who run several agent tools keep the instructions they share across those tools in the shared agent configuration root (`~/.agents/AGENTS.md`, or `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME`) that `dsh-skill-filesystem` already scans for skills. Those instructions reached DSH only when the person copied or symlinked them into the harness home, which duplicates one source of truth into DSH-owned data and leaves no way to tell which copy a session lo...

name: 2026-10-06-web-desktop-plugin-identity-compatibility
title: Preserve Web and Desktop plugin identities across experimental consolidation

attrs.decision:
The moved packages retain the published names declared by the [experimental naming policy](../../../../scripts/experimental-package-policy.ts). That typed directory-to-name map is the sole maintained inventory of unprefixed experimental names; under the [unprefixed naming decision](2026-11-04-unprefixed-experimental-package-names.md), every new experimental package joins it. Package manifests, consumers, installation checks, and bundler checks agree with it; a missing, moved, or duplicated entry is rejected. [Experimental status](../../../../packages/experimental/README.md#status) remains independent of spelling, Official discovery, and explicit selection.

Existing badge, Ralph, and native delegation row IDs remain valid Host row selectors. New isolation groups and newly introduced capabilities retain their new IDs. Later user layers still replace configuration or disable rows. Selecting an optional bundle is still explicit: a patch targeting an absent row does not select its bundle.

Compatibility protection covers Web and Desktop profiles, including existing native provider package identities, selections, configuration, and authentication. Native bundles insert ordinary Host row...
attrs.problem: Moving a capability into the experimental directory changes its ownership and support classification. Renaming its published package or an existing configuration row additionally changes how installed profiles refer to that capability. Those identity changes can make a working Web or Desktop customization require edits unrelated to the capability's behavior.

name: 2026-10-08-desktop-shell-configuration
title: Desktop shell configuration independent of the Host

attrs.decision:
Electron main owns `userData/desktop/settings.json` independently of Host startup and Cordis evaluation. The test authentication popup switch uses this file; the [Desktop reference](../../../../apps/desktop/README.md#local-desktop-settings) owns its fields and behavior.

Ownership follows runtime dependencies: Electron-owned functions needing configuration before Host startup or while the Host is unavailable use shell configuration. Host plugin settings, including shared Web/Desktop preferences, continue to use Cordis. Displaying a setting in Desktop alone does not justify shell ownership. A unified settings interface can use separate storage owners.

The `desktop` subdirectory groups shell configuration without relocating existing files. The [shortcut decision](2026-09-20-device-local-shortcut-preferences.md) retains ownership of `userData/keybindings.json` and its persistence semantics. The [shared Web application decision](2026-09-10-desktop-web-wrapper.md) still governs Host composition and profile configuration.
attrs.problem: Desktop updates and native recovery can run before the Host starts or while it is unavailable. Depending on Host configuration prevents these functions from resolving their preferences when needed. A shared settings page does not identify which process owns each preference.

name: 2026-10-08-persistent-ptc-sandbox
title: Retained PTC processes follow file policy

attrs.decision:
`persistent-in-memory` starts its Node process through the same sandbox provider as `per-call`. A retained owner uses one resolved mode, workspace root and Session identity until release. The [memory decision](2026-09-23-best-effort-persistent-ptc.md) owns retained values, failure recovery and package composition; this note owns file authority.

The [PTC-owned cleanup decision](2026-10-09-ptc-owned-policy-cleanup.md) supersedes this note’s permission-setter completion and cleanup-ownership decision. Permission changes commit synchronously; PTC owns immediate cancellation and waits internally before subsequent execution. The tools package keeps Agent ownership and omits the owner for temporary escalations.

An approved one-time escalation omits the state owner and receives a fresh temporary environment. Its process is released before the call returns. It cannot access standing variables, and its declarations do not survive. The standing environment keeps its original policy and variables. Nested tools continue to apply their own permissions and approvals.
attrs.problem: Retaining JavaScript variables does not require broader file access. A process that outlives one execution can also outlive a one-time approval or a Session policy change. File-policy changes must invalidate retained environments and begin stopping their file handles and background work.

name: 2026-10-09-composer-command-chip
title: Claimed commands as atomic composer chips

attrs.decision:
A claim replaces the leading trigger span with `CommandChipNode`, an atomic inline `DecoratorNode`, followed by the token's argument separator as an ordinary text node.

- The node carries the `CommandClaim`, including its submit closure. History restores nodes with their fields, so undoing a chip deletion restores the claim. JSON export writes the token text; JSON import yields a plain text node because the closure has no JSON form.
- The detect projection counts the chip as one U+FFFC, so trigger detection never re-reads the command name. The clipboard projection is the token without its separator. The chip is not a reference occurrence. `EditorProjection.command` is the claim of a chip that opens the document.
- Outside a submit transaction, the machine's claim follows the document: `draft-changed` carries the leading chip's claim, so deleting or displacing the chip releases the claim and a history restore re-enters claimed. name: 2026-10-09-cua-shared-native-helper
title: Shared native CUA process with Agent-scoped state

attrs.decision:
One user shares a native service per executable content digest across Agents and Hosts. A version lock elects the service; an additional canonical-executable-path lock prevents different builds published at one path from running together. Locks remain held until process exit. The managed startup command hands service lifetime to its client connections, and the last connection's completed cleanup ends the service. The diagnostic stdin/stdout entry proxies to this same service.

The service runs as a signed application launched through LaunchServices. Directly spawning the executable inherits its launcher’s TCC responsibility, so it cannot give the helper independent system permissions. A launch lock serializes discovery and startup. Complete signed applications use immutable content-addressed directories: replacing an executable used by a live process would violate both path-lock ownership and code-signature integrity. Ad-hoc builds can require fresh grants when their code hash changes; a stable bundle identifier alone does not preserve those grants. Source checkouts can keep grants with the [development signing identity](2026-10-29-cua-dev-signing-identity.md). Installed packages r...

Two live helpers at the same path repeatedly replace each other's connections even when their screenshot requests are sequential. Byte-identical executables at distinct real paths complete sequential and concurrent captures; two symlinks to one executable reproduce the failure. A per-request lock cannot isolate retained system connections.

name: 2026-10-09-operator-scoped-connect-handshake
title: Peer-scoped connect handshake

attrs.decision:
Browsers retain their existing signed Cookie, root launch-token exchange, the Token Provider's shared Peer with owner principal and `interactions: 'answer'`, and recovery behavior. Only API callers create independent Peers through `GET /connect?token=<launch-token>&interactions=answer|none`. The endpoint is API-only, defaults to `none`, rejects invalid or repeated declarations with 400, and retains Host/Origin checks and token authentication. It returns 302 with the Remote Mux destination and an API Cookie.

### Admission and ownership

- Connect publishes the API Peer before returning. Its signed API Cookie carries the authority, Peer id, and issue/expiry interval; interaction participation belongs to the live Peer, not another credential field. Browser v1 Cookies remain valid and always select the shared Peer. API v2 Cookies select only an existing independent Peer.
- HTTP validates the Cookie and finds its Peer without waiting for a WebSocket. Connect, HTTP, and WebSocket require no cross-transport readiness ordering.

name: 2026-10-09-ptc-owned-policy-cleanup
title: PTC owns policy-change cleanup waits

attrs.decision:
Permission setters commit synchronously. Success means the selected policy is recorded; it does not guarantee that operations admitted under the old policy have completely stopped. This replaces the completion requirement and cleanup ownership in the [retained-process sandbox decision](2026-10-08-persistent-ptc-sandbox.md), whose confinement and one-time escalation rules still apply.

PTC observes committed Session mode changes. The tool bridge immediately cancels affected complete calls, including pending approvals and nested tools. A later PTC call waits for canceled predecessors to settle before resolving the latest standing policy. The Node provider immediately invalidates affected processes, including idle environments, starts cleanup, and retains the cleanup Promise internally. A later program waits for that cleanup; failed cleanup remains retryable and prevents process reuse. Unchanged modes preserve environments. Tool-registry and provider unload remove their observers and await owned work.
attrs.problem: Stopping a retained Node process and its nested tools can take longer than recording a new file policy. Making permission setters await that cleanup spreads PTC lifecycle requirements into unrelated callers, including Webhook Session creation, and adds cancellation windows to those callers.

name: 2026-10-09-stored-credential-precedence
title: Stored credentials take precedence over the launch environment

attrs.decision:
**A stored credential wins for every provider.** `LocalCredentialProvider` resolves a reference in this order:

```text
$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml        (provider-managed, written by set/unset)
> inherited process environment    (fallback; the provider never writes it)
> <invocation cwd>/.env            (fallback; the provider never writes it)
> $DSH_HOME/.env                   (fallback; the provider never writes it)
```

name: 2026-10-10-user-text-json-nodes

attrs.decision:
The composition is business registration, lazy candidate matching, a single reconciliation loop, readonly JSON nodes, and business-owned keyed renderers. Initialization and Facts refresh use the same algorithm; they differ only in which query caches remain valid.

### Rule roles and original coordinates

Every rule provides an ID, finite order, and synchronous `match(text, from, context)`. Each call returns its nearest eligible node with `start >= from`, or no candidate anywhere in the remaining original text. It returns one node, not all matches or a replacement document. The original string and UTF-16 offsets remain intact: a search cursor does not create a new word, line, or quoted-token boundary. Matching depends only on original text and Facts, not previously selected node payloads.

Each matcher resolves its own alternative spellings by earliest start and then its documented same-start choice; Session labels choose the longer match. A matcher cannot replace a consumed prefix with the remainder of an overlapping candidate. Each business owns its grammar, payload, and renderer; the generic evaluator has no Session, file, skill, or command branches.

name: 2026-10-12-exclusive-conversation-matches
title: Exclusive Conversation matches

attrs.decision:
A match result may claim its event on the Definition's target:

```ts
interface ConversationMatchResult {
  readonly id: string
  readonly role: 'start' | 'update'
  readonly exclusive?: true
}
```

- **Dispatch.** `ConversationNodeAssembler.dispatchInput()` evaluates every match of one event into two reused arrays before accepting any, then settles claims. - **Failures.** Two claims on one target, or a claim from a Definition without a target, throw during dispatch and name the event, its `seq`, and the claiming Definition kinds.
- **Scope.** A claim belongs to one event and comes from `match()`, so a Definition claims only the events it recognizes. The generic Definition declares nothing.

title: Headless jobs omit the interactive credential store

attrs.decision:
The shipped headless bundle disables the base `credentials`, `authorization` and `deepseek-account` rows. API-key adapters already support compositions without the credentials service and resolve through the launch snapshot: process environment, invocation-directory `.env`, then Harness-home `.env`. name: 2026-10-12-session-projection-registration-handles
title: Asynchronous projection registration and retained readers

attrs.decision:
`SessionProjectionRegistry.register` returns an awaitable registration for a typed handle. Domain owners await it during activation before exposing dependent operations. Function plugins retain their namespace exports and use asynchronous `apply`; services use their initialization hook. Each domain service keeps its definitions and handles internal and exposes methods returning business data. Consumers depend on that service rather than registering its definitions or receiving projection readers. This supersedes the optional first-access acquisition and disposer-return details in [the mandatory-reader decision](2026-08-19-session-projection-mandatory-seam.md), while retaining its mandatory-state and cropped-client-view rules.

A handle owns one reference to a shared definition and its per-Session cells. Its disposer releases global participation exactly once; the final release removes the unit from live drives and snapshots. Checkpoints keep each Session's last cell of the released unit until its key registers again: the registry no longer advances that cell, while a retained handle read still advances it forward, so a writer that runs after the owner unloads still stores the state...

name: 2026-10-13-cua-continuous-hover
title: Continuous CUA hover without cross-call ownership

attrs.decision:
An explicit Window exposes `mouseMove` for coordinates or an observed element ID. The result reports `hoverRoute` and `systemPointerMoved`. It never presses a mouse button. With session approval, system-pointer movement also works on disabled controls. Completion, AX reads and screenshots do not restore a previous pointer position. Successive calls can visit intermediate points before entering a popup. Clicks deliver button events at their target without an off-window priming click. The [input-routing decision](2026-10-13-cua-hover-routes-and-coordinates.md) requires foreground and mouse-hit checks for system movement. It never activates or raises the app implicitly. Other input or window changes can race that check.

The [shared helper](2026-10-09-cua-shared-native-helper.md) serializes complete individual operations. It grants no application ownership across calls. Earlier arrival, a retained app object and Session lifetime do not establish task priority. Waiting for the model does not reserve the application. Explicit task coordination determines any required execution order.
attrs.problem: Hover interactions span movement, delayed content, observation and input inside a revealed region. A request cleanup that restores the pointer, or a click that first presses outside that region, can dismiss the content even when nobody else sends input.

name: 2026-10-13-cua-hover-routes-and-coordinates
title: Background hover and screenshot coordinates

attrs.decision: By default, native hover uses a same-window element or ancestor advertising both `AXShowAlternateUI` and `AXShowDefaultUI`. Entering its revealed descendants preserves the parent UI; leaving restores it. An unavailable route returns `HOVER_UNAVAILABLE` by default. With `requireSystemPointerApproval` enabled, the first explicit `mouseMove(target, { useSystemPointer: true })` asks the user. Each physical move requires an explicit request, even after approval. The live session remembers the decision until the session closes or DSH restarts. This lets a caller reach pointer-tracking controls even when the same target also advertises AX alternate UI. The Host selects real input only for a move that requests it and meets the approval policy. Physical movement leaves the visibility of previously revealed controls to the application, so switching routes cannot dismiss a target before dispatch. An AX action failure propagates because received effects may be uncertain. The result records the route and whether the system pointer moved. System movement requires the selected foreground app and AppKit's mouse hit test, which excludes input-transparent overlays. No route grants [cross-call owners...
attrs.problem: Hover-only controls can sometimes be revealed without moving the user's pointer. Treating every hover as a system movement unnecessarily disturbs that pointer. Screenshot pixels also differ from native window points after Retina capture, attachment normalization or model-request resizing; making the model convert them duplicates provider geometry rules.

name: 2026-10-13-team-identity-runtime-context
title: Subagent identity in required runtime context

It derives identity from `ctx.subagents.rootOf(agent)`: the root sees its own Session id, and descendants see their own, direct parent, and root ids. An unavailable root is reported explicitly. Optional-context suppression and Team mode do not remove identity. Agents receive messaging and discovery guidance only while the root is available and each corresponding standard tool is admitted. Team task policy stays in the shared system prompt; task state remains a tool query.

The loop owns logging, retained-snapshot comparison, and re-admission after compaction. A changed role appends the current full runtime-context snapshot after inherited history; unchanged retained context adds no message. No Team-specific retention state, event type, or log migration is introduced. Existing recorded reminders remain historical messages.

This supersedes only the initial-task identity decision in [Agent Teams](../feature/2026-08-05-agent-teams.md#team-identity). [Task-board wait coordination](2026-10-19-team-task-board-inbox.md) keeps ordinary inbox waiting ...

Identity must reflect the current subagent tree while keeping shared system instructions uniform.

name: 2026-10-15-agent-teams-as-subagents
title: Agent Teams teammates are subagents

attrs.decision:
Use one subagent identity: the Session id. The existing `description` tool argument supplies the catalog label and display text; descriptions may repeat and never address an agent. Creation accepts no member name, reserves no names, and adds no catalog payload version.

[Tree-wide communication](2026-10-16-tree-wide-agent-communication.md) authorizes an exact live sender within one root tree and preserves the actual sender’s id. Interruption retains ancestor authority and id addressing.

Every root Agent and its descendants form the Team identified by the root Session id. Team creates no agents and contributes task tools and task policy. Ordinary subagent controls supply required identity, discovery, messaging, interruption, and inbox waiting. Parent and fork children receive identical tool schemas and shared policies.

Task ownership uses `ownerId`; root reassignment accepts itself or any reachable continuable descendant. Historical roster records remain decode-only. Team persists task changes without ending inbox waits or starting idle turns; [inbox-only waiting](../simplification/2026-10-29-inbox-only-agent-wait.md) owns wake behavior. Historical `team/message/*` records remain ...
attrs.problem: Teammates already use the subagent runtime for creation, Session identity, catalog membership, capacity, cold resume, settlement, and interruption. A separate Team roster duplicates identity, provisioning recovery, and teardown. Team-scoped messaging and control tools shadow the standard subagent tools, forcing profiles to disable ordinary delegation and making fork tool schemas diverge from their parent.

name: 2026-10-16-separate-instruction-chain-budgets
title: Separate byte budgets for the user-global and project instruction chains

attrs.decision:
The renderer splits the loaded files into the user-global and project chains, keeping their order, and renders each under the same `maxBytes`: omit the broadest files, truncate the last file, then fall back to the compact intro, to the notice with an empty heading, and to the notice alone. The project chain keeps the result it has when rendered alone; user-global files are omitted or truncated only beyond their own budget, except in the fallback below.

When all files fit `maxBytes` together, or only one chain has files, the output is unchanged byte for byte. Otherwise one `<system-reminder>` frame of at most twice `maxBytes` holds the merged notice when a file was omitted or truncated, one intro when a chain kept its frame, and the rendered sections in loaded order, with user-global files first in a baseline. If a chain renders without a frame and the merged frame would exceed that bound, all files render as one chain under one `maxBytes`, which can omit a user-global file that fit its own budget; this needs a budget of a few hundred bytes or a notice that nearly fills or exceeds `maxBytes`. Reconciliation batches apply the same split.

The `maxBytes` key and the baseline identity...
attrs.problem: `dsh-agent-instructions` rendered the user-global and project files as one chain under one `maxBytes`, the rule of the [original workspace-context decision](../../archived/feature/2026-06-24-workspace-context.md). Rendering omits the broadest files first, and user-global files are the broadest, so a large project chain removed them: under the shipped 65,536-byte budget, 20 KiB user-global, 30 KiB project root, and 20 KiB nested files rendered without the user-global file.

name: 2026-10-16-steering-batch-start-in-definition-state

name: 2026-10-16-tree-wide-agent-communication
title: Communication follows the subagent tree

attrs.decision:
`list_agents` starts at the caller's live root and lists that root and all reachable continuable descendants, including the caller. Full names remain relative to the root. The existing parent catalogs remain authoritative; no Team directory is stored separately.

`send_message` accepts another root or continuable member of the same tree. The sender must be the exact live root or a resident continuable subagent. Cross-branch delivery verifies the target descriptor and creation catalogs, then restores only the target under the Team root. Final inbox admission rechecks the sender and root. Cancellation or rejection before acceptance releases the new target instance; accepted input follows normal Agent persistence.

The existing Agent registry records runtime ownership by the Team root. Creation parent ids and catalogs preserve ancestry for discovery and interrupt authority. A member finishing or being released affects only its own instance; Team-root shutdown joins all startup and cleanup. This removes ancestor restoration, parent retention, and recursive disposal without adding a Team runtime registry. Saved target presets and permission events supply restoration configuration.

name: 2026-10-18-session-list-summary-projections
title: Serve Session-list rows from a summary key set

The todo entry is `SessionProjectionSummaryExcluded<TodoItem[]> | null`, because an intersection with `null` would absorb the null member.

Four of those views are never rendered by a row: the whole-log turn outline, the whole-log conversation figures, the current todo list, and the host-wide image limits. name: 2026-10-18-websocket-permessage-deflate
title: Compress the Remote stream WebSocket with permessage-deflate

attrs.decision:
The Gateway Config adds `websocketCompression: 'none' | 'deflate'`, defaulting to `'deflate'`, and passes the resolved boolean into the mux. The mux constructs `WebSocketServer` with these transport options and decides compression per outbound frame:

| Option | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Frame compression threshold | `1024` characters of the JSON text, decided in the mux send path | `ws` ignores its `threshold` option while context takeover is enabled ([upstream 41ae5631](https://github.com/websockets/ws/commit/41ae5631)), so the mux passes `compress` per frame; frames below 1,024 characters (most token-level `item` frames) stay uncompressed and out of the zlib pool |
| `perMessageDeflate.zlibDeflateOptions.level` | `1` | Interactive frames value latency over ratio; the HTTP gzip default in this repository is also `1` |
| Context takeover | `ws` default (enabled both ways) | Best ratio for repetitive JSON; no per-message dictionary rebuild |

The mux constructor takes one options object carrying `heartbeatIntervalMs`, `streamInboxBytes`, and `compression`, because the Gateway resolves the config vocabulary and `stream-server.ts` does not learn `'none' | 'deflate'`.

The mux itself is the implemented [Remote duplex stream](2026-09-19-remote-duplex-stream.md) design; this note adds one transport option to it. The Host's HTTP surface already exposes `compression: 'none' | 'gzip'`; before this option the WebSocket had no equivalent, so the link stayed uncompressed.

name: 2026-10-19-client-plugin-package-assets
title: Client plugin package assets served by URL

A Client plugin package keeps raw images under `src/client/assets/`. The shared preset emits each referenced image under `lib/assets/` and turns the reference into a synchronous `require.asset(<document-relative URL>)` call on the bundle's module loader; the package publishes the emitted files with `"exports": { "./assets/*": "./lib/assets/*" }` and `lib/assets` in `files`; the client-modules Host serves them at `/plugins/<package>/assets/<emitted path>`.

Both compile to a `require.asset(reference)` call whose argument is the same reference; a stylesheet becomes string literals joined with those calls, which run when its injected text is built. The module system answers each call through its `resolveAsset` option, which returns the reference unchanged unless a carrier supplies one. The emitted file name inserts the content revision, the first 12 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-1 digest of the bytes, before the extension, so one URL always names one content:

That route served only `client.js` and package-local chunks, so an image that plugin code referenced had to be embedded in the bundle as a base64 data URL, and an image used by a stylesheet needed a package-level build plugin that rewr...

name: 2026-10-19-cua-profile-consent-storage
title: Durable Computer Use consent within one profile

attrs.decision:
The CUA owner uses the existing domain storage service, with one domain per canonical profile directory. It stores long-term grants and conversation decisions by native application identity. Conversation IDs scope permission without turning it into permission for every conversation. The native identity policy remains owned by [bundle-ID consent](2026-10-25-cua-bundle-id-consent.md); this note replaces only that note's storage and restart-lifetime choices.

Every operation opens fresh domain state while holding the profile's existing file-lock primitive and closes the domain before releasing the lock. Native dispatch and revocation use a separate lock for the selected application. Storage reads and unrelated applications remain available during a native call. Revocation cancels this process's affected work first, then commits after other processes' already-admitted operations have finished. A completed revocation therefore leaves no operation using the old authority. App-wide revocation generations and per-conversation decision revisions prevent an old handle or delayed answer from restoring revoked access.

The JSON backend remains the shipped default. The domain name contains the ...
attrs.problem: Application grants stored as plugin configuration make each authorization change depend on configuration reconciliation. Process-local conversation decisions also disappear when the same conversation resumes after a restart. A shared in-memory storage handle cannot observe another process revoking permission.

name: 2026-10-19-file-drag-plugin-ownership
title: File drag ownership outside the application layout

attrs.decision: The [file-drag plugin](../../../../packages/client/ui-file-drag/README.md) owns generic file preparation, browser transfer tokens, retained original files, desktop bridge selection, and transient failure feedback. Consumers receive preparation and error callbacks through their slot or Factory injection. The plugin registers its feedback through `shell.overlay`; layout declares the generic slot and has no image dependency. The shared image primitive owns gestures and cancellation. Images are the first consumer, while MIME naming and transport accept other files.
attrs.problem: Image dragging spans conversation images, sidebar previews, and composer drop targets. Original files must survive source unmount during a drag, and failures must remain visible after the originating panel closes. An application-root image provider puts feature state in layout and makes independent image entries depend on an undeclared React ancestor.

name: 2026-10-19-pi-ai-system-reminder-fallback
title: Pi-ai system reminder fallback

attrs.decision:
The pi-ai adapter uses the prepared model's existing `supportsMidConvoSystemMessages` capability mapping. It preserves native system messages on capable models and converts each non-empty later system message into a user message wrapped in `<system-reminder>` otherwise, before pi-ai receives the context. Leading system text remains in the initial prompt. Message order, repeated updates, and existing text-block concatenation remain intact. Durable messages retain their original roles.

The fallback belongs to the adapter because it depends on the selected protocol capability. Prompt admission remains owned by the agent loop, which consolidates system-prompt updates on routes without native support; this fallback only handles later system messages present in the supplied request.
attrs.problem: Pi-ai concatenates later system messages into the initial prompt for models without native mid-conversation system support. Later system messages supplied to the adapter therefore invalidate the preceding conversation cache prefix.

name: 2026-10-19-team-task-board-inbox
title: Team task boards share ordinary subagent waits

attrs.decision:
The subagent tree is the Team. Ordinary controls own required identity, communication, discovery, interruption, and `wait_agent`, independently of the optional task board. Team tools own task policy, without adding it to ordinary subagent compositions. Team owns task storage, dependencies, and compare-and-set commands. Assignment accepts the root or any discovered continuable descendant. Historical roster records grant no authority; the Team panel shows tasks and ordinary navigation owns members.

The wait-signal decision is superseded by [inbox-only Agent waits](../simplification/2026-10-29-inbox-only-agent-wait.md). Tree ownership, task durability, and historical non-authority remain unchanged.

Task state remains in the existing journal. Ordinary tool results record what the waiting model observes. Historical roster, mailbox, and task generations remain readable and unchanged. This partially supersedes the roster and wait decisions in [Agent Teams](../feature/2026-08-05-agent-teams.md) and [subagent teammates](2026-10-15-agent-teams-as-subagents.md). Their task durability and single-identity rationale remain active; [required runtime identity](2026-10-13-team-identity-runtime-co...
attrs.problem: The subagent tree already supplies identity, discovery, routing, and lifecycle. A second Team roster can grant assignment authority from stale history and duplicates member navigation. Team-wide status waits observe unrelated activity and miss input already pending for the caller. Persisting task-board wakeups as messages adds unread state and message schemas even though the task journal already owns the state to inspect.

name: 2026-10-20-new-session-blank-reuse-by-preset
title: New Session reuses a blank Session, matching a requested preset

attrs.decision:
Only the Client (`ui-workspace`) changes; the Host is unchanged:

- `startSession` without options takes the reuse path again and follows the same rule as `openWorkspace`, `connectWorkspace`, and `startSession` with options.
- `createInWorkspace` names the first unstarted, unarchived blank Session that is still a Workspace member. A request that names a preset skips a blank whose listed preset (`projectionValues.agentPreset`) is a different one, while a blank with no listed preset remains eligible; a request without a preset may name any blank, which the Host switches to its default preset. The Host creates a Session when no blank is eligible.

As a result, New Session returns to the original blank Session with its unsent draft, and preset flows such as the Creator entries do not take over a blank that lists another preset, so an ordinary draft is not moved under Creator. No persisted state is added, and the Client does not read the preset roster.
attrs.problem: In 0.2.0-rc.2, New Session (the sidebar button, the Workspace "+" button, and the shortcut, all calling `uiWorkspace.startSession` without options) reused the Workspace's first blank Session. PR #5775, first released in `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.2`, changed it to create a fresh Session and Agent on every call, so that New Session composes the current preset definition after the user changes one instead of keeping a reused blank's earlier composition ([upgrade guide](../../../../docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1...

name: 2026-10-20-ptc-script-evaluation-and-retention
title: PTC Script evaluation and state retention

attrs.decision:
The Node provider adds `executionMode: vm-script` and a separate `scriptPersistence` option, defaulting to false. `PtcRuntime.programFormat` describes accepted syntax; `retainsState` describes owner-scoped memory. Consumers use the latter for persistence controls and guidance. Existing `per-call` and `persistent-in-memory` configurations retain their meanings and defaults.

This extends the mode-naming decision in [best-effort persistent PTC](2026-09-23-best-effort-persistent-ptc.md), whose ownership, non-durability and recovery decisions remain active. The Node provider selects its evaluator once and shares managed process mechanisms across temporary and retained lifetimes. AsyncFunction, REPL and Script remain separate evaluator implementations, so process reuse does not define syntax.

VM Script uses a separate realm inside the managed child process. Top-level await uses the Node.js v26.6.0 REPL transform, with Acorn and acorn-walk supplying parsing and traversal. Detection precedes native compilation because non-strict Script can compile `await` as an identifier. The adapted visitors traverse computed method keys without entering method bodies. The source retains upstream attri...
attrs.problem: Program syntax and memory lifetime answer different questions. A consumer may need Script declarations and completion values while requiring either a fresh environment or retained references. Inferring memory lifetime from REPL syntax prevents that choice.

name: 2026-10-20-session-team-mode
title: Team availability is selected per Session

attrs.decision:
The base bundle loads the Team service and task tools, and the Web bundle loads the Team UI. The packages belong to the subagent and client product groups. A saved root-Session selection gates task tools and Team guidance throughout the tree, and the shared board in the root conversation; new Sessions default off. Ordinary subagent creation, communication, and navigation remain available.

The model and reasoning menu owns the user’s selection. The root conversation’s Subagent panel displays members above shared tasks. Disabling Team keeps the journal and children; re-enabling restores the board. Historical task boards without a saved selection stay enabled. Profile loading removes the retired optional bundle selection, retaining row overrides.

Headless deployments may set `agent-team.defaultEnabled` to save an initial selection for a new root during startup creation. Saved selections take precedence, and resumed Sessions retain their mode even when no selection exists. Ordinary forks initialize independently; subagents share their live root’s selection. Creation identifies subagents by their Session origin because activation ownership is registered only after creation listeners s...
attrs.problem: A plugin-level Team switch requires users to change the shared profile before choosing collaboration for one conversation. It can disable another Session’s capability and leaves a second control beside the Session selection. Ordinary tasks still need their existing tool catalog, and disabling collaboration must not discard task history or children.

name: 2026-10-20-workspace-tree-state-per-pane
title: The workspace tree is per-pane state drawn inside each file tab, and the plugin mounting it decides where files open

attrs.decision:
### The tree is drawn inside each file tab, and its state is kept per pane

`ui-sidebar-right` supplies `useTabInfo().panel` with the containing pane's `id` and `isFloating`; moving a tab updates those fields without changing `tab.id`. It supplies no pane lifetime. `ui-sidebar-files` owns each pane's tree state, visibility, width, listing, directory watches, scroll, and last revealed file. The navigator and toggle are Session-scoped Component Factories; `ui-sidebar-documentpreview` renders them inside the tab's content row and header, with stable positions across loading states. The docking kit does not acquire a files-specific overlay or layout rule.

A pane's records follow the tabs whose navigator last drew there, using each tab's `signal`. A replacement in the same pane retains the records. A moved tab uses its destination pane's records; a pane without records starts hidden at the default width. Tab-owned preview scroll is independent of that tree state. Records are released after their last associated tab closes or draws the navigator elsewhere.

Directory watches follow visible drawings rather than retained records. Hidden trees hold no Host directory watch; showing them aga...
attrs.problem:
Reading several workspace files needs a tree beside their previews without losing expansion, loaded levels, width, scroll, or keyboard position on every tab switch. The dock mounts only the selected tab's body, so a component instance cannot own the state shared by a pane's file tabs.

A floating panel holds one tab. A preview's file picker must replace that tab in its panel, while the files page must remain available and open content in the dock. A covering tree must close where content is navi...

name: 2026-10-21-context-menu-contributions
title: Context menu contributions

attrs.decision:
[Context menus](../../../../packages/client/ui-context-menu/README.md) own typed target families, contribution resolution, and callback lifetime. Feature plugins register actions through the same service available to external Client plugins. Plain presentation fields let a renderer consume resolved actions without loading contributed React components. Existing Session and tab Slots remain in feature-owned adapters, preserving those extension positions.

[File actions](../../../../packages/client/ui-file-actions/README.md) own original-content transfer separately from menus and image components. Saving retains original encoding; clipboard interoperability may require PNG conversion. A browser download supplies no local path, so reveal requires a verified Host file or the destination returned by a native save.

The menu plugin contributes `useContextMenu` through the existing Slot root binding. Its ordinary `getTriggerProps` factory centralizes DOM gestures while business owners still provide captured targets. Plain children receive props or existing delegates; a separate React Context or utility package would duplicate the established lifetime and injection mechanism.
attrs.problem: Session and tab menus already accept React Slot entries. Reusing only those entries would require external plugins to supply React components and would leave action discovery, target capture, and cancellation coupled to each trigger.

name: 2026-10-21-replaceable-icon-sprite
title: Replaceable product icons through an SVG sprite

attrs.decision: Each product glyph weight is one sprite symbol, `dsw-icon-<glyph>-<weight>`. ui-primitives keeps the default SVG documents as `ICON_SYMBOLS`; an icon component keeps its export name, `size`, and `className`, and renders an `<svg>` box with one `<use>` of its symbol. ui-theme keeps one hidden sprite in the document whose `<symbol>` children come from the active theme's `ThemeDefinition.icons` replacements or the defaults. Artwork reached through `<use>` inherits `currentColor` and CSS custom properties from the use site, so a replacement can be multi-color, can paint with `--dsw-*` color tokens, and follows light and dark palettes without separate values.
attrs.problem: Long-term skin customization needs themes to replace icons, not only colors. Product icons were React components that drew inline SVG paths, so a theme registered through `ctx.theme` could recolor them through `currentColor` but could not change their artwork. About 150 Client files import these components.

name: 2026-10-21-schedule-rule-storage
title: Schedule rule storage and shared recurrence

attrs.decision:
Use `schedule` version 2 with `compatibleVersions: [1]`, retaining its backend routing, envelope, and whole-unit layout. Extend the existing accepted-version policy to authoritative JSON and SQLite units; reads leave storage unchanged, and the next write commits the current stamp with its data. Add `rrule` to the six existing record kinds and evaluate every kind normally. Remove the standalone store importer, import marker, placeholder RRULE, and parallel Session-bound management API. Move reusable Cron and RRULE parsing and bounded occurrence arithmetic into `dsh-util-time`; Schedule owns records, targets, delivery admission, history, and errors.

An explicit target wins. Without one, read an existing `sessionId` as a Session target; otherwise reserve a stable `new_once` target. Optional new metadata receives read defaults without rewriting storage. Every successful edit writes the current row format without `sessionId`. Custom timing accepts either RRULE or a five-field Cron expression with an explicit zone; UI labels name neither syntax. Model guidance continues to teach RRULE.

This partially supersedes [standalone schedules](2026-09-17-standalone-schedules.md): its target, exe...
attrs.problem: Host tasks already use the versioned `schedule` domain. A second domain, importer, and placeholder RRULE duplicate timing and storage authority. Cron and RRULE should be supported timing types rather than separate generations of the task API.

name: 2026-10-21-session-history-stream-and-snapshot
title: Session snapshots, passive subscriptions, and Web aggregation

attrs.decision:
`SessionController` is the single Session Remote Service. It owns ordinary `HistoryController`, `StateController`, and `WebController` instances, not three additional Cordis Services or Remote namespaces. The implementation separates six operations: history snapshot and observation, projection snapshot and observation, and state snapshot and observation. Follow and Wait compose those capabilities for their callers; the existing `page` entry forwards to the history reader.

### Reads and subscriptions

History reads return chronological records, `hasMore`, and an inclusive cursor. An omitted `throughSeq` selects the observed log end; `beforeSeq` selects older records without changing that read cut. Projection reads return exact sequenced values, sequence-free cache hints when migration is required, or null when the Session is absent. Live projection reads avoid persistence metadata access.

`usingObservation({ sessionId, projection }, signal, callback?)` acquires the existing disposable SessionObservation. A callback borrows it until the callback settles; without a callback the caller owns disposal. Ordinary history, state, and Wait output reads do not request projections. Follow, e...
attrs.problem: A point read, an event subscription, and a Web conversation opening have different lifetimes. Combining them inside one history controller makes passive observation perform unnecessary reads and gives each aggregate its own acquisition logic. Reading before subscribing also creates a gap that requires another read to repair. The APIs need independent operations that can compose without losing events or duplicating ownership.

name: 2026-10-22-deepseek-official-model-listing
title: The official DeepSeek route follows the official model listing until its catalog is customized

attrs.decision:
- [`llm-deepseek-api-key`](../../../../packages/llm/llm-deepseek-api-key/README.md) follows `GET https://api.deepseek.com/models`, authenticated with the API key in `x-api-key`, only while the Messages origin is `https://api.deepseek.com` and `models` equals the built-in catalog. - Loading, refresh, fallback, merging, and the client-version gate are the [account route's](2026-09-24-deepseek-account-remote-model-catalog.md): a first access waits up to `modelsTimeoutMs`, a listing older than `modelsMaxAgeMs` refreshes in the background on the next access, a failure keeps the last good listing or the built-in catalog, and the cache lives in memory, keyed by endpoint and key fingerprint.
- A customized `models` list wins whole: it replaces the catalog and stops listing requests. - Switching between a customized catalog and the listing invalidates the cache from a `loader/volatile-update` listener, so Restore default...
