A model the DeepSeek API added reached API-key users only through a release, while the account route already followed the service's `GET /models` listing at the same origin. Unlike the account route's catalog, the official route's catalog is user-editable: the Models page stores an edited catalog in `models`, and a gateway behind `baseURL` declares its model...

name: 2026-10-22-subagent-target-user-controls
title: User controls address the target subagent

attrs.decision:
Browser prompts and `interruptByUser` address only the target child Session. Each Remote method explicitly declares that Session as its access resource; the Gateway checks the invocation's principal before attachment admission, restoration, or cancellation. A global or parent Session grant does not imply a child Session grant. Policies decide whether to grant both actions, either action, or inherited access. Same-process user interruption trusts its caller and does not accept a wire-supplied principal.

Prompt delivery derives the live root from the resident Activation or verified persisted creation edges. Only the cold target resumes; its creator can remain offline. Shared delivery retains exact live root checks, shutdown admission, cancellation, capacity, and final inbox acceptance. A root Session is not a target of the browser subagent prompt endpoint. User interruption addresses a resident Activation without persistence reads or restoration; an absent target remains a no-op, and interruption preserves parked input.

Model messages retain the exact live sender and same-tree rule from [tree-wide communication](2026-10-16-tree-wide-agent-communication.md). Model interruption retai...
attrs.problem: A browser knows the subagent it is displaying, but requiring its direct creator and a continuable marker makes every control caller repeat history metadata. A caller-supplied parent id checks address consistency without establishing the caller's identity or permission. Calls that resolve only the global access resource also cannot express a grant on one target Session.

name: 2026-10-22-subagent-tool-owned-communication
title: Subagent tools own communication guidance

attrs.decision:
`tool-subagent-control` owns messaging instructions and parent addressing. Its logged runtime context gives delegated children their direct creator’s name from `ctx.subagents.namesOf()`, explains when to send findings, and states that sending does not finish a turn. The context is emitted only for delegated children when the plugin’s own tool definition is admitted in the current scope and step; roots and ordinary Session forks receive none. Communication guidance follows inherited history without changing the shared system prompt or tool schema.

The manager owns result delivery. Local activations with `delivery: 'parent'` receive automatic-result guidance even without messaging tools; caller-owned activations receive no parent-delivery promise. Settlement timing, recipients, output, and suppression of closing text after a final message to the parent remain unchanged. Tool visibility grants no messaging authority.

This supersedes the Symbol identity and initial-task communication-guidance choices in [adjacent messaging](2026-08-27-adjacent-agent-steer-messaging.md). Its message attribution, fixed Steer delivery, and rejection of a separate report operation remain active. The inte...
attrs.problem: The continuation manager inspected a Symbol on the standard messaging tool before adding tool instructions and parent addressing to the initial task. This coupled orchestration to one tool implementation and made result-delivery guidance depend on tool installation. A published internal entry point carried both that marker and a host prompt adapter used only by tests.

name: 2026-10-23-independent-session-forks
title: Ordinary forks have no durable creator relationship

attrs.decision:
Ordinary forks preserve their complete selected prefix, `isSeeded`, `inheritedEventCount`, and inherited end-seed marker, but record no source id. Subagents retain their direct creator, including when their backend copies history. `origin: subagent` supplies coarse classification; a valid own-range descriptor separately supplies continuation identity. Historical parent metadata remains readable and unchanged. Runtime Agent ownership remains governed by the [explicit identity decision](2026-08-31-explicit-agent-runtime-identity.md).

The V4 reader permits another Session's delivery id only inside the validated inherited range. Own-range markers still require the current id, and every active-generation `throughSeq` must precede its marker. These checks do not require a persistent source relationship.
attrs.problem: Using `parentSession` for both copied history and delegation makes an ordinary fork appear to be a subagent. Consumers can emit false child-start notifications, hide resumable sessions, or impose source-relative ordering. Removing the writer alone leaves historical ordinary forks misclassified and exposes a V4 reader assumption: inherited delivery acknowledgements require a parent id even though the validated seed range already identifies copied events.

name: 2026-10-23-store-scoped-image-reads
title: Image reads use attachment-store access

attrs.decision:
Session membership is not an image-access restriction. After connection authentication and Gateway permission checks authorize `session/attachment`, every caller may read any image in the same attachment store using a complete `ImageAttachmentRef`, including objects referenced only by other Sessions or not referenced at all. The request retains `sessionId` for the existing Session resource permission check. After that check passes, the handler does not require that Session to exist and does not return `session/not-found` solely because it is absent. No identity receives a separate history-scanning path.

The Client already holds the message's complete image reference and sends it as `attachment` beside `sessionId`. Session Controller delegates directly to the existing `AttachmentStore.readImage(ref)`. Its local provider validates the canonical ID, derives the path within its object directory, verifies SHA-256, and compares the actual format, byte length, width, and height with the supplied reference. A missing, unreadable, corrupt, or mismatched object rejects the operation. No Session history is needed to recover the reference.

The response preserves the supplied reference. Its o...
attrs.problem: Historical image loading read the requesting Session and searched its event content for every uncached attachment. The search established that the Session referenced the image; it did not locate the bytes, whose storage path already follows from the content-addressed ID. This added work proportional to history length to each image read. The reported loading delay also involved uploads; this finding alone does not identify all of that delay.

name: 2026-10-25-cua-bundle-id-consent
title: macOS consent shared by bundle identifier

attrs.decision:
macOS application consent uses the exact, case-sensitive native bundle identifier. The helper hashes `macos:bundle-id:` followed by that identifier into `CuaApplicationId`. When a bundle identifier exists, installation paths, versions and signatures do not distinguish grants. Otherwise, the helper hashes `macos:executable-path:` followed by the canonical executable path. Both identities support saved access; path identities survive restart and in-place updates, while a different path requires a new decision. Conversation decisions and saved grants retain the scopes and revocation behavior of [profile consent storage](2026-10-19-cua-profile-consent-storage.md).

This supersedes the executable/signature identity choice in [application consent](2026-09-26-cua-application-consent.md); that note still owns enforcement and human decisions. The running process path comes from the operating system. A valid runtime bundle identifier does not depend on path-query success. Missing paths omit optional grant metadata; they never substitute a cached catalog path. When both bundle identity and process path are unavailable, consent fails with the path query cause. Process identity must still be ve...
attrs.problem: Users who install multiple versions of one application want one permission decision for that software. Executable paths split those decisions, and signing checks exclude unsigned development applications from saved access.

name: 2026-10-26-cross-deployment-office-kit
title: Office skills in every deployment with one Office Kit package

attrs.decision:
The [Web bundle](../../../../packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml) and the [SDK bundle](../../../../packages/bundle/sdk-app/cordis.patch.yml) mount [`skill-office`](../../../../packages/skill/skill-office/README.md) in Desktop, ordinary `dsh web`, and the SDK. This supersedes the mounting decision of [progressive Office skills](2026-09-27-progressive-office-skills.md); its skill structure remains current, and the [on-demand Office tools](2026-10-31-native-office-tool.md) replace its shell execution.

Every deployment reads the Office skills from the `skill-office` package's `assets/`, which hold only `SKILL.md` files. The Host reads them with ordinary file reads: Desktop's Electron Host reads them inside `app.asar`, and the SDK executable embeds them, so no carrier copies the skills to a separate resource directory. A composition selects another directory through `assetRoot`, or overrides individual skills with same-name filesystem skills.

The bundled Python environment ([`tool-workspace-dependencies`](../../../../packages/skill/tool-workspace-dependencies/README.md)) mounts only in Desktop and in the SDK when a primary runtime is available. `skill-office` declares `pythonEnvi...
attrs.problem: Office skills were mounted only by Desktop and the Python SDK, so ordinary `dsh web` users could not create or inspect Office documents with the same guidance. Each deployment located LibreOffice Kit differently: the conversion provider, the skills, and the Desktop shell each held their own lookup, and an absent Kit made the conversion row fail to load. A Python SDK executable without its downloaded Office sidecar, or a source checkout without native engines, is a deployment that lacks Kit, not ...

name: 2026-10-26-session-writable-directory-effects
title: Session writable-directory effects

attrs.decision:
The sandbox-policy service owns effect-scoped directory registrations keyed by live Session identity. Configured grants remain shared; runtime grants apply only to their named Session. Each resolution captures the active union, and existing request-context logging records the directories advertised to the model. Resume and fork require new registrations rather than restoring authority from historical text.

Registration disposal affects subsequent operations, not already-resolved calls or running processes. This deliberately permits persistent terminals and PTC environments to retain their launch grants until they stop. The requirement is to update ongoing Sessions' future executions without coordinating process cancellation or losing retained state. This narrows the different-policy reuse restriction in the [retained PTC sandbox decision](2026-10-08-persistent-ptc-sandbox.md) for additional directories only; mode-change invalidation and one-time escalation cleanup remain unchanged.

Missing, non-directory, and symlinked extra paths stop execution with `SandboxInvalidRootError`, which identifies the path and its problem. Silently skipping a path would hide an invalid grant and let ...
attrs.problem: Memory plugins need agent writes outside the workspace without granting every Session the same directory. Deployment-wide roots cannot express a plugin enabled for only one Session or a grant that ends when that plugin unloads.

name: 2026-10-27-plugin-cli-absolute-paths
title: Plugin CLIs by absolute path in runtime context

attrs.decision:
Each app plugin registers its CLI's absolute path with `ctx.cliAccounts`, the Service of [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-cli-account`](../../../../packages/connector/cli-account/README.md). The Service registers required runtime context at the `PLUGIN_CLIS` context order, without interpolation, that tells the model to run the CLI by that path. For a skill whose scripts call the CLI by name, which applies to DingTalk and WeCom, the context also tells the model to prefix only the commands that run those scripts with `PATH="<directory>:$PATH"`, and never to export PATH or run the CLI by name. On Windows, where the shipped compositions mount `tool-pwsh` instead of `tool-bash`, the text uses PowerShell syntax: the call operator, `& '<path>'`, and the prefix `$env:PATH = '<directory>;' + $env:PATH`. Skills tell the model to use the path from the current runtime context. The plugin's own sign-in, status, and sign-out commands spawn the same path through the Service's command runner.

The harness changes no command environment: Bash, PowerShell, the sandbox, persistent terminals, and hooks run as they do without these plugins. Tencent Meeting registers its platform executable, `dist/tmeet-<platform>`. ...
attrs.problem: CLI app plugins such as Feishu, WeCom, DingTalk, and Tencent Meeting install a vendor CLI outside PATH. The upstream guides, the CLIs' own messages, and the DingTalk and WeCom skill scripts call it by name. The model must run the plugin's installation, not another installation or none, and the harness should not change how model commands run to make that happen.

name: 2026-10-28-upstream-skills-runtime-download
title: Runtime download of upstream skills

attrs.decision: Each of these plugins keeps only its DSH-authored entry `SKILL.md`, pins the upstream files by repository, commit, kept directory, exclusions, license file, total size, and a digest of the kept files, and registers both with `ctx.upstreamSkills`, the Service of [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-upstream-skills`](../../../../packages/connector/upstream-skills/README.md). The Service downloads the commit archive from GitHub when the plugin loads, keeps the directory and the license file, verifies them, publishes them in `$DSH_HOME/cache/<plugin>`, and lists the entry skill with that directory as its base directory. The plugin shows the download state beside the account state. Its check reads only the account and restarts a failed download without waiting for it: the CLI account runtime runs one operation at a time, so a check that waited for a slow GitHub download would also hold sign-in. Each archive source has `skillsTimeoutMs` to deliver the whole archive, and reading stops once the kept files exceed the pinned size. A plugin's `skillsDir` points at prepared files for tests and offline installations, and the Service's `skillsUrls` replaces the archive host for every plugin.
attrs.problem: The WeCom and Tencent Meeting plugins index guides that their vendors publish only in their GitHub repositories: 180 files, about 1.75 MB, for WeCom and 11 for Tencent Meeting. A copy in this repository dominates each plugin's diff and every upstream update, and the plugins' npm packages would publish DeepSeek's copy of another company's content. DeepSeek does not publish such copies.

name: 2026-10-29-cua-dev-signing-identity
title: Development signing identity for source-built CUA helpers

attrs.decision:
The Host builds source checkouts as a development variant with bundle identifier `com.deepseek.harness.computer-use.dev` and name `DSH Computer Use Dev`, in `DSH Computer Use Dev.app`. The macOS privacy list and the helper’s reported launch application use the bundle filename, so that filename also includes Dev. The release variant and its packaging are unchanged. Grants stay with the helper application launched through LaunchServices, as the [shared helper decision](2026-10-09-cua-shared-native-helper.md) requires.

`sourceSigning` belongs to the macOS provider and accepts only default `ad-hoc` or `{ identity, keychain }` selecting an existing certificate and absolute keychain path. Builds do not create, unlock or remove identities. Developer credentials stay separate from the user-facing DSH home, which stores only the certificate selection; the shared `cua` package owns no macOS signing configuration.

The [developer signing skill](../../../skills/dsh-cua-macos-signing/SKILL.md) guides Agents through creating, reusing and unlocking an isolated identity under `~/.cua-macos-keys/`, then selecting its fingerprint and keychain path in user configuration. The tool stores a random pas...
attrs.problem: Source checkouts compile `DSH Computer Use.app` with an ad-hoc signature. macOS stores Accessibility and Screen Recording grants for a bundle identifier with the designated requirement of the granted code, and an ad-hoc requirement is the code hash. Every changed build and every other worktree therefore needs new grants, and these builds shared the release helper's bundle identifier and replaced its grant entry.

name: 2026-10-29-retained-ptc-interruption
title: Retained PTC interruption

attrs.decision:
The host revokes execution authority immediately and requests cooperative stop over the existing control channel. The runtime rejects pending bindings; the original `run()` response confirms that evaluation has settled. Revocation is a one-way notification. The ordered pipe and single active evaluation determine notification ownership; RPC requests associate replies with callers. Acknowledgment permits reuse of the VM and retained objects; earlier mutations remain. Callers await acknowledgment or fallback process cleanup before starting another evaluation.

The host bounds acknowledgment with `stopGraceMs`. Missing or failed acknowledgment terminates the managed process range and awaits cleanup. Results retain the original timeout or cancellation kind and report whether variables survived. Confirmed termination allows a fresh environment on the next call; failed cleanup blocks reuse until host release succeeds. Explicit reset, disposal and policy invalidation terminate immediately. Reset uses the existing release path and exposes no additional model tool.
attrs.problem: Terminating a retained Node process on every timeout or cancellation loses unrelated application objects and imported modules. A control handler on the evaluation thread cannot stop a synchronous loop. The [in-memory execution decision](2026-09-23-best-effort-persistent-ptc.md) still owns disposable state and Session behavior; this decision replaces its timeout and cancellation cleanup policy.

name: 2026-10-29-web-provider-selection
title: Web provider selection - independent menus over registered providers

attrs.decision:
Users choose search and fetch providers independently from the Host's registered provider lists. The shipped composition fixes no search provider, so search follows the conversation's model route, and selects local HTTP fetch for fetch; the DeepSeek Search and Fetch APIs follow the conversation's DeepSeek credential.

### Registered providers are observable; availability is not

`WebSearchProvider` and `WebFetchProvider` carry an optional `title`, the provider's display name, and an optional localized `description` of what the provider suits and what it costs or cannot do. `ctx.web.listProviders()` returns `{ search, fetch }`, each a registration-ordered list of `{ id, title?, description? }` entries, and the `web` Remote namespace exposes it as `web/listProviders`. Every registration and disposal emits the payload-free `web/providers-changed` event after the registry changes; the web service contains listener failures, so an observer cannot veto a registry change. [dsh-api-remotes](../../../../packages/api/remotes/README.md) mounts the namespace and forwards the event, and Clients re-read the list after each notification and reconnect.

The lists include providers whose `available...
attrs.problem: The web service selects search and fetch providers through two independent fields, `web.searchProvider` and `web.fetchProvider`. A settings control that writes both at once ties fetch billing and target access policy to the search choice, and a control that offers only the DeepSeek choices it knows cannot select a provider that another plugin registers. A picker over registered providers needs the Host to report them, and the [web capability seam](2026-06-24-web-capability-seam.md) has no availa...

name: 2026-10-29-windows-file-tool-directory-grants
title: Windows additional directory grants stay in file tools

attrs.decision:
On Windows, the [session directory effects](2026-10-26-session-writable-directory-effects.md) authorize extra directories only through the harness filesystem checks used by `write` and `edit`. The process provider ignores extra roots and retains its workspace and private-temp permissions. The ACL package, runner arguments, and workspace SID remain unchanged. POSIX process backends continue to honor extra roots.

Windows process support for extra roots is deferred until a better sandbox backend can enforce it without extending the ACL customization. Model context explicitly distinguishes file-tool grants from Windows process permissions.
attrs.problem: Memory plugins need session-specific writes to directories such as `~/.dsh/memory`. Extending Windows process access through ACLs requires managing persistent filesystem grants and token identities for changing directory combinations, increasing reliance on a backend with existing enforcement limitations.

name: 2026-10-31-native-office-tool
title: On-demand Office tools for rendering, conversion, and recalculation

attrs.decision: The [`tool-office` package](../../../../packages/document/tool-office/README.md) exposes `office_render`, `office_convert`, and `office_recalculate` as three on-demand Host tools. Each tool states its parameter rules in its own JSON Schema: `office_render` accepts document paths, page or slide `pages`, worksheet `sheet` and `range` selection, and `dpi`; `office_convert` accepts all nine output formats (`pdf`, `docx`, `odt`, and `txt` for Word; `pdf`, `xlsx`, `ods`, and `csv` for Excel; `pdf`, `pptx`, and `odp` for PowerPoint) plus `sheet` for CSV output (required when the workbook has several sheets); and `office_recalculate` accepts `xlsx` and `ods`. Together the three declarations total ~1,813 characters, paid only in Sessions that load an Office skill. They call the [Office kit](../../../../packages/document/office-kit/README.md) service, which loads Kit in the Host process through its `src/locate.ts` resolver and runs every operation through the queue, concurrency limits, byte reservations, and cache that Office previews use. Tool requests use `foreground` priority, the class of an open preview, so background prewarming cannot starve them. The SDK composition mounts `tool-offic...
attrs.problem: Office operation skills ran the LibreOffice Kit CLI through ordinary shell commands, as [progressive Office skills](2026-09-27-progressive-office-skills.md) decided. Kit's native engine starts helper processes, Workers, and font caches that the shell sandbox and PTC permissions restrict, so the same render could succeed in one deployment and fail in another. Each deployment had to publish a standalone Node executable and a CLI path into the skill body, which required Node and CLI configuration, ...

name: 2026-11-02-subagent-catalog-names
title: Subagent names live in the creator's catalog

attrs.decision:
The Session id remains the only execution identity for routing, authorization, persistence, task ownership, and navigation. A name is a model-facing reference to it.

Each new child has a name that is unique among its creator's children. The name is a field of the `subagent/catalog` entry that the creator already appends when it creates the child, using catalog payload version 3. Local and parent-delivered external creation write it; caller-delivered external runs enter no catalog and take no name. A name is 1–32 lower-case letters, digits, or hyphens starting with a letter, and is never `lead`. A 36-character UUID therefore never parses as a name. Omission selects the first free `agent-N`. An explicit name already held by a sibling fails with `DUPLICATE_AGENT_NAME`, and an invalid name fails with `INVALID_AGENT_NAME`.

The creator reserves the name synchronously at admission, before startup awaits anything. The reservation lives in process memory beside the creator's committed catalog names and is released when the catalog entry commits or startup fails. Task assignment copies the immutable full name into optional `ownerName` beside `ownerId` in the same task event. Task reads use...
attrs.problem: Models coordinate subagents through `send_message`, `interrupt_agent`, `list_agents`, and Team task owners. Those tools addressed every member by a 36-character Session id. Models copy such ids poorly: they cannot recall which id belongs to which task, they mistype ids, and every listing, receipt, notice, and identity statement spends tokens on them. Descriptions explain responsibilities but repeat and cannot address a member. Models need short, readable references that survive restarts and reso...

name: 2026-11-03-hoc-slot-kind
title: Add the `hoc` slot kind so plugins can wrap owner content in layers

attrs.decision:
[The Markdown fence keyed hoc slot note](2026-11-05-markdown-fence-hoc-slot.md) records why hoc layers take an optional dispatch `key`, may omit `children`, share compiled chains per key, and stay registered after a crash.

Add a fifth kind: `hoc`.

| Item | Contract |
|---|---|
| Declaration | The parent entry's `children` lists `{ kind: 'hoc', scope }`; `SlotMap` declares `kind: 'hoc'` |
| Rendering | `renderSlot(key, owner, { children, entryKey })`; `only` / `fallback` / `hookContext` are unavailable; omitted `children` renders the layers around nothing; omitted `entryKey` applies only wildcard layers |
| Registration | Required `id`, optional `key`, `order`, and `priority`; a layer without `key` is a wildcard serving every dispatch, a layer with `key` serves only that `entryKey`; the cell is `(key or wildcard, id)`, and within one `id` an exact-key layer replaces the wildcard layer for that key; the same cell at the same `priority` throws, a different `priority` shadows |
| Nesting order | Ascending `order`, then `priority`, then registration order; lowest outermost |
| Layer props | Every layer receives the same owner props plus the framework-supplied `children` (the next inne...
attrs.problem:
The home whale plays when blank space is clicked. Its canvas must paint below the content, and `.scrollBody` fills the whole body, so the canvas itself never receives clicks; only an ancestor of the content does.

No existing slot kind lets a plugin become an ancestor of the content:

| Kind | Behavior | Why it is not enough |
|---|---|---|
| `single` / `list` / `keyed` | Render the occupant at an owner-chosen position | The occupant is a sibling of the content |
| `chain` | The elected entry re...

name: 2026-11-03-session-workspace-root
title: Session workspace root

attrs.decision:
A Session works in one directory, and only Host operations move it. The model-facing `working_directory` tool and the `cwd` parameter of the delegation tools are removed; the model reaches a subdirectory through paths and the shell's per-call `workdir`. `header.cwd` remains the immutable original project: Session identity, workspace grouping, and the recovery destination. `dsh-working-directory` owns the directory and has one read, `get`: relative paths resolve from the directory, and it is the workspace root that consumers bound writes, file views, and discovery by. Every change the service records, through `set` or the recovery of `ensure`, is a `workspace-root/change`.

`workspace-root/change` is a new ordinary event type, recorded as a same-version persistence change in the [acknowledgement](../../../../docs/persistence-changes/2026-11-13-workspace-root-change.md). `working-directory/change` stays in the event vocabulary, deprecated and without a writer. Readers ignore a stored one: the same event recorded the model's `cd` and an entered worktree, and most stored ones are a `cd`, since few stored Sessions ran the worktree plugin. A Session that holds them resumes in its origina...
attrs.problem: A Session that enters a Git worktree records only a changed current directory. The `working_directory` tool recorded the same event for a model's `cd` into a subdirectory or out of the project, so a consumer could not tell a model-moved cursor from a changed checkout: a file view, a change summary, or a write boundary either followed every `cd` or stayed on the original project. Usage did not justify the cursor: in 58 recorded Sessions of one developer that offered the tool, the model called it ...

name: 2026-11-04-unprefixed-experimental-package-names
title: Name new experimental packages without the experimental prefix

attrs.decision:
New experimental packages use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>` and never the `experimental` prefix. Each one is declared in `EXPERIMENTAL_PACKAGE_NAME_EXCEPTIONS` in the [experimental package policy](../../../../scripts/experimental-package-policy.ts), because isolation checks and plugin-record ownership recognize an unprefixed experimental name only through that map. Promotion moves the package and removes its map entry; its npm name stays the same.

Existing packages with the prefix are listed in `LEGACY_PREFIXED_EXPERIMENTAL_PACKAGE_DIRECTORIES`. `pnpm run constraints` rejects the prefix in any other directory and rejects a listed directory that no longer holds a prefixed package, so the list can only shrink. A legacy package is renamed when it is promoted; renaming it earlier needs the release and migration evidence that the [plugin identity decision](2026-10-06-web-desktop-plugin-identity-compatibility.md) requires.

This decision replaces the deferred cleanup that the plugin identity decision recorded, which gave every experimental package the prefix. The [package rules](../../../../packages/experimental/AGENTS.md) state the naming rule for authors.
attrs.problem: An experimental package named `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-<name>` must be renamed when it moves to a product group. The rename changes every import, dependency entry, module declaration, and profile file that names the package, so promotion carries a migration that is unrelated to the capability's behavior.

name: 2026-11-05-client-module-metadata
title: Client metadata and renderer-owned stylesheet installation

attrs.decision:
Client artifacts contain `id` and `factory`, with optional `meta` and a `chunk` name for dynamic package-local chunks. `meta()` returns resource descriptions; `stylesheets` is an optional path-keyed record whose values expose independently evaluated `text(context)` functions. Resource paths identify stylesheets, not components. There is no stylesheet dependency field.

Modules owns JavaScript exports, module identity, owner ids, and observed dependency edges. It retains metadata functions without evaluating them and publishes generic module-record changes. Renderer owns metadata/text caches, dependency-ordered stylesheet collection, path deduplication, and main-document nodes. It explicitly installs existing resources before React mounting, updates them on module changes, and releases styles after the root unmounts. Component lifetimes do not own styles.

Static library builds keep their index artifact as ordinary ESM with all imports and dynamic imports for final shell assembly, and add the `__$dsh_client_module_manifest` export carrying the same manifest. The boot shell itself remains ordinary ESM. Modules wraps the existing carrier loading hook in its built-in Main environment; ...
attrs.problem: A script's execution environment need not be its presentation document. CSS injection embedded in JavaScript factories couples those destinations and makes module loading responsible for DOM cleanup. Inferring stylesheet ownership from React components would add component-level tracking without reliable source-file identity.

name: 2026-11-05-cua-scoped-surfaces-and-input
title: CUA scoped surfaces and separated input capabilities

attrs.decision:
`CuaSurface` declares operations shared by application and window objects; `CuaApp` and `CuaWindow` extend it with their own operations. One base factory builds the surface, and the derived factories inject scope parameters plus `requireAccessibility` and `requireKeyboard` checks. The shared base never branches on a capability that exists only for applications.

Provider startup capabilities are static. Platform, supported methods, application-level accessibility, keyboard scopes, browser support, and coordinate space are fixed when the provider is installed. The native `getCapabilities` RPC reports runtime permissions and session lock only; `installCua` merges the two layers for the model-visible result. The neutral RPC is a common operation representation, not a capability inventory; provider guidance names the actions its platform supports.

Keyboard input keeps keys and modifiers separate: `pressKey(key, modifiers?)` presses and releases one key while holding the listed modifiers, and its keyboard modifier list is a plain string array defined by the provider. `sendKeyEvent(key, direction)` sends exactly one key-down or key-up without an implicit counterpart. A caller can theref...
attrs.problem: Application and window objects share accessibility operations, but only an explicit window can capture or deliver pointer input. Duplicating shared methods on both factories creates two implementations to keep aligned. Moving application-only capability checks into the shared base makes window behavior depend on an application-level decision. Keyboard input has the same problem at a smaller scale: a chord string combines a key and its modifiers, and a complete-keystroke method cannot express a m...

name: 2026-11-05-harness-error-dependency-free-base
title: Keep the HarnessError base in a dependency-free package

attrs.decision:
`HarnessError` lives in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-error` (`packages/util/error`), a package with no dependencies that contains only the base class. `dsh-llm` depends on it and re-exports the same class from its entry, so existing `import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'` statements keep working and both import paths name one constructor, which keeps `instanceof` checks consistent. LLM-specific failure codes and helpers such as `isHarnessError` stay in `dsh-llm`.

New code imports `HarnessError` from `dsh-error` when the importing package does not otherwise need `dsh-llm`, so a package that needs only the base takes no dependency on the LLM runtime. Packages below `dsh-llm`, such as `dsh-attachment`, can extend the base without a cycle.
attrs.problem:
The tool registry records a failed result's `error.name` and `error.code` only when the thrown value is `instanceof HarnessError`, so every expected failure must extend the one shared class; copying its `code` field is not enough. The [archived structured-error-taxonomy note](../../archived/architecture/2026-06-11-structured-error-taxonomy.md) placed the base in `dsh-llm` because `dsh-llm` was then a leaf that every package already imported, so the base added no dependency edge.

`dsh-llm` stopp...

name: 2026-11-05-markdown-fence-hoc-slot
title: Dispatch Markdown fences by language through a keyed hoc slot

attrs.decision:
### Developer-facing API

The API has two parts: a delegate that hands each fence to its owner, and a keyed hoc slot through which plugins register language renderers.

| Part | Contract |

name: 2026-11-09-explicit-ptc-output

attrs.decision:
TypeScript `run_code` programs select text, objects and images through top-level `inspect(...values)`. Arguments are rendered independently: strings appear directly, and other values use Node's object formatting without depth, array-length or string-length preview limits. Inspection displays undefined properties, Error objects and circular references; requiring lossless JSON for display would interrupt subsequent work after tools have already executed. Images can occur inside arrays or objects. The runtime Image's custom inspection hook collects images reached by Node's formatter; each formatting call owns its collector. One output sequence preserves the relationship between explanatory text and selected images.

The tool executor requests `discardCompletion: true`, so completion values are discarded before JSON validation and serialization. This is a consumer choice: direct runtime and workflow consumers retain completion values when their protocols require them. name: 2026-11-12-cua-program-tool-without-presets
title: CUA program tool for Agents without a preset

attrs.decision:
When `agentPreset` is a preset ID, only Agents on that preset receive raw `cua`. Every other Agent receives `cua_run_code`, including Agents without a composed preset and every Agent of a composition without the preset registry. The registry is an optional dependency of the provider: the provider recomputes the tool form of each live Agent when the registry loads or unloads, and without the registry no Agent counts as being on the configured preset. `agentPreset: false` still registers raw `cua` globally and creates no program runtime.

This partially supersedes [CUA programs outside the PTC preset](2026-11-09-cua-program-tool.md), which gave Agents without a composed preset neither tool. That note still owns the program tool's runtime, its initialization, and the choice of one tool form per Agent. It also changes one consequence recorded in [What stays host-plane once presets own the agent plane](2026-08-10-host-plane-ownership-after-presets.md), where an Agent that joined no preset received no tool. That note still owns the rule that entry points join Agents explicitly and that no check rejects an Agent for joining no preset.

A native CUA provider configured with a preset ID registered no tool for those Agents, so its default configuration and the Computer Use bundle had no effect there. `agentPreset: false` supplied only the raw `cua` tool. A Host whose model calls ordinary tools directly had no configuration that supplied `cua_run_code`.

name: 2026-11-13-ptc-output-truncation
title: PTC output truncation without execution cancellation

attrs.decision:
Captured output has bounded retention. Exhaustion preserves an ordered prefix, discards subsequent output and sets `outputTruncated`; it does not cancel execution or discard retained variables. Existing deadlines, cancellation, heap limits and control-message limits still apply. Finalization prioritizes the required completion value or bounded failure diagnostic within the combined payload budget. Truncated diagnostics preserve their failure kind. Required completion values remain lossless and fail if they cannot fit.

This supersedes only captured-output termination and diagnostic reclassification in [typed tool returns](../feature/2026-07-20-ptc-typed-tool-returns.md), and overflow-driven state disposal in [retained PTC](2026-09-23-best-effort-persistent-ptc.md). Those records still own lossless values and retained-state lifetime; [explicit output](2026-11-09-explicit-ptc-output.md) still owns inspection and image projection.
attrs.problem: Stopping a program because its logs exceed the output budget can interrupt a sequence of external actions. Earlier effects remain, but the caller cannot tell which later actions ran. Repeating the program to obtain less output can repeat those effects. A full log budget can also hide a subsequent exception by replacing its kind with an output-limit failure.

`SessionPersistence.identity` is a `Symbol('sessionPersistence')` created once per service instance. name: 2026-09-29-reused-blank-runs-requested-preset
title: A reused blank Session runs the requested preset

attrs.decision: `session.create` returns a Session for a new conversation. A named `sessionId` is a reuse candidate that the Host verifies: it must not have started a turn, must belong to the requested directory, must be an unarchived member of the requested Workspace, and must not be written by another owner. name: 2026-09-30-job-session-lifecycle
title: Persist owned job lifecycle facts

attrs.decision:
The local provider captures `job/registered` and `job/settled` facts for owned jobs, retaining the registry's epoch-millisecond timestamps, original owner, producer kind, label, and optional creating tool call. A UUID-backed `JobId` identifies both live controls and historical records across registry restarts and copied history. Unowned work has no Session journal.

The terminal record distinguishes a producer report from forced bookkeeping: `producerReported` is true when `JobHooks.done` fulfills, and false when that promise rejects or teardown cancellation throws. It reports fulfillment, not independently confirmed resource release. Missing terminal records remain incomplete and are not reconstructed from later reads or process restart.

Facts are appended synchronously at the registry commit before live hub reactions and completion waiters resume. Recording errors warn independently: already-started work still has its control id, and a failed journal append cannot prevent cleanup or release of waiters. The Session's ordinary persistence and SDK notification paths own delivery after append. SDK `run()` results cover bounded observation windows and can receive a settlement whose r...
attrs.problem: SDK consumers receive Session events, while job registration and settlement previously existed only in the live registry. A background tool can return before work finishes, and output collection can happen much later or never. Tool invocation times therefore cannot reconstruct a job's execution interval. Runtime-local ids also repeat after a registry restart.

name: 2026-09-30-session-list-host-fairness
title: Time-sliced Session-list work

attrs.decision:
[ApiSessionList](../../../../packages/api/session-controller/src/list.ts) uses one monotonic deadline for classification and summary generation. It yields only after elapsed work exhausts the configured `listWorkSliceMs`, then starts a new deadline after the wait. The optional deployment setting defaults to 16 positive integral milliseconds. Small lists have no forced final yield or no-op asynchronous helper. Cancellation is checked per row, after each yield, and before returning; no partial list is returned.

Every row remains synchronous. Live rows precede queued cold rows before the stable activity sort; the list promises no cross-Session atomic cut. A cold row already queued before an attachment remains cached, and Client mutation replay plus [cached/sequenced precedence](../architecture/2026-09-19-projection-cache-listing-identity-and-cached-rows.md) reconcile the newer live state. No projection data or validation is omitted.
attrs.problem: Large cached projection states can monopolize the Host while a Session list is assembled. Yielding after every row avoids that batch stall but adds thousands of event-loop round trips when a list contains many cheap rows. Row count alone is not a useful scheduling budget.

name: 2026-10-10-background-shell-command-display

The terminal component receives the original call's `background` flag from Start and combines it with the call's `running` value: `background=true` and `running=true` mean that the launch call is still in progress. When the acknowledgement arrives, `background` stays unchanged and `running=false` leaves a static command; it does not describe the background job's running state. name: 2026-10-22-series-start-unchanged-prompt-prefix
title: A series start with an unchanged prompt keeps the surviving system node

`SystemPromptProjection.project` re-baselines node 0 only when the effective text must move: an incapable route, an empty rendering, or a series start whose latest surviving non-empty node text differs from the rendering. When the route is in-history, the rendering is non-empty, and the latest surviving node already holds it, the projection returns no updates and the node stays where the cached history carried it. name: 2026-10-25-shared-preset-delegation-tools
title: Shared preset delegation tools

attrs.decision:
Each tool-subagent instance registers its definition in its owning composition. Agents sharing a preset revision inherit that registration. Switching presets changes ancestry; it requires no per-Agent installation or tool-change reconciliation. Provider availability and the owning composition's disposal control registration lifetime.

Tool configuration validates its own fields, allowlist consistency, required services and provider capabilities. Candidate preset documents are not read during registration, for either Host-mounted or preset-mounted tools. The delegation executor validates the model's selection against the allowlist; child startup resolves the selected id against the current registry. A later declaration can therefore satisfy a previously unavailable target without reinstalling the tool. Independent selection and restoration retain the [spawn preset semantics](../feature/2026-09-20-spawn-agent-preset-selection.md).

name: 2026-10-26-malformed-charset-declaration
title: Malformed charset recovery prefers UTF-8

attrs.decision:
`decoderForCharset` preserves valid single-label declarations and the absent-header UTF-8 default. If a declaration is unsupported as a whole, it checks its comma- and whitespace-separated labels for UTF-8, including standard aliases. A match selects a fatal UTF-8 decoder; otherwise the declaration fails before the response body is read and the provider cancels the stream.

The provider decodes once. Recovery rejects invalid UTF-8 with `WEB_UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE` and preserves the decoding error as its cause. Only an actual byte-cap truncation enables streaming decode, which omits an incomplete suffix and keeps `truncated: true`. Complete responses, including those exactly at the cap, validate the final sequence at EOF.

UTF-8 recovery is an explicit heuristic, not proof of the original encoding. The bytes `C2 A9` represent `©` in UTF-8 and `漏` in GBK; repeating them preserves that ambiguity at any length. The provider accepts that ambiguity for UTF-8 recovery but does not extend it to arbitrary legacy-encoding guesses.
attrs.problem: A response can declare `charset=utf-8,gbk` over readable UTF-8 HTML. Passing that entire parameter to `TextDecoder` rejects the page before reading it. Compatibility needs an explicit encoding preference because successful decoding alone cannot identify the server's intended encoding.

name: 2026-10-28-forge-git-session-permissions
title: Session permissions for Forge Git queries

attrs.decision:
Git inspection uses the Session's resolved sandbox mode and subprocess provider. Full access requires no sandbox backend; confined modes retain their enforcement and never retry unconfined. The Session remains the authority for filesystem permissions, including workspace-write access. Query commands do not request repository mutations.

Local patches and statistics apply command-local Git configuration to disable clean/process filters without changing user configuration. Environment entries preserve subsection names containing equals signs. Existing hook, fsmonitor, external-diff, textconv, optional-lock, and lazy-fetch restrictions remain; submodule queries show commit changes without scanning internal dirty files. Configuration read failure stops the comparison; the changes view reports the filter configuration failure separately from oversized diffs and offers a retry. These restrictions follow the informational-diff approach in Codex while retaining DSH's execution-world and cancellation ownership.
attrs.problem: The [Forge panel](../feature/2026-10-09-forge-panel.md) forces read-only confinement even when a Session grants full access. On hosts without a usable sandbox, its checkout and local changes remain unavailable while the Session's shell works. Background queries also reach repository-configured executable helpers through working-tree comparisons.

name: 2026-10-28-plugin-install-failure-diagnostics

The command line itself stays module-local: `installBundle` strips it off the plain `PackageResult` it returns, so no second wire field appears.

name: 2026-11-01-locked-python-runtime-deploy
title: Locked Python runtime deployment

attrs.decision:
The Python builder uses pnpm's default deployment, which derives a dedicated production lockfile from the workspace lockfile and installs it frozen. This replaces only the deployment strategy in the [single-executable distribution decision](../architecture/2026-07-10-single-file-executable-sdk-runtime-distribution.md); its runtime architecture and carrier layout remain active.

Deployment retains the source lockfile's peer settings, including `autoInstallPeers: true`. Frozen installation preserves already resolved versions and peer relationships instead of resolving new registry peers. Forcing `autoInstallPeers: false` conflicts with the derived lockfile settings and fails frozen installation. The resulting tree need not equal the legacy tree resolved with peers disabled; selected dependencies must come from the locked graph. `verify-runtime-closure.ts` independently requires explicit workspace peers and preset plugins before deployment, and `verifyStagedDependencies` rejects missing direct dependency directories after materialization and deduplication.

The scrollport's reach tracker travels in the handler object. name: 2026-11-13-draft-attachments-across-session-switches
title: Draft attachments across Session switches

attrs.decision:
**A draft with attachments holds its Session's scope.** While a composer draft has attachments and its Session is not removed, the input hub holds the Session with a `draft` reference that keeps no event connection, as [Session retain facets and recently viewed Sessions](../architecture/2026-11-15-session-retain-facets-and-recent-views.md) defines. Switching away and evicting the Session from the recent views therefore keep the same composer shell and its attachments: an active upload keeps running, a failed upload keeps its in-place retry, and a pasted image keeps its bytes in memory. Removing the last attachment, sending it, or removing the Session releases the hold; scope teardown then releases every attachment the draft still holds.

**A reload reports discarded attachments instead of restoring them.** On `pagehide`, the input hub marks each Session whose draft holds attachments in browser storage; a back-forward cache restore clears the marks. A composer mounted with a mark shows the "add them again" notice.
attrs.problem: Switching to another Session and back emptied the composer's attachment rail while its text survived (issue #5070). The Session scope disposer released every attachment the retiring composer held and revoked image previews, and nothing could rebuild them.

name: 2026-07-06-approval-seam

name: 2026-07-10-parallel-tool-call-execution
title: Parallel tool-call execution by per-call safety

attrs.decision:
Each tool may provide an optional `isConcurrencySafe(args)` classifier. It is synchronous and pure: it examines only the current call's parsed arguments and performs no I/O or mutation. Only an explicit `true` opts in; a missing classifier, invalid arguments, a thrown classifier, or any other return value makes the call exclusive. The canonical type contract lives in the [tool data structures](../../../../docs/subsystems/tools.md).

The classifier is deliberately unary. Returning `true` is the tool's promise that this call may overlap with any sibling call that also returns `true`; the scheduler does not compare calls or prove that their resource accesses are compatible.

The unary classifier remains input-sensitive. A tool may classify a read-only operation as parallel and a mutating operation as exclusive. The interface cannot express relational rules such as "these writes are safe only when their paths differ," so a call whose safety depends on a sibling remains exclusive.

name: 2026-07-12-subagent-persona-tool-filter-and-depth

name: 2026-07-20-ptc-typed-tool-returns
title: Typed tool returns in PTC mode

attrs.decision:

name: 2026-08-31-cross-process-session-write-lease
title: cross-process session write lease

attrs.decision: `SessionWriteLease` (packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/lease.ts) holds a kernel lock on `session.lock` beside the log for the whole life of a write handle: POSIX takes a non-blocking `flock(2)` through the prebuilt `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system/flock` binding, and Windows holds a named kernel semaphore (count 1) derived from the canonical lock path (`CreateSemaphoreW` in src/win32.ts beside the existing koffi bindings) — a kernel object with no filesystem footprint, destroyed with its last handle. Contention maps to `SessionAlreadyOwnedError`; the kernel releases the lock when the holder's descriptor or handle closes, including on any process death, so a crashed holder never blocks a successor and no expiry bookkeeping exists. A live but wedged holder keeps the lock until its process exits: expropriating a stalled writer was rejected because its resumed appends would tear the log, and on POSIX removing the lock file remains the explicit forfeit for that case. Because a POSIX lock names an inode rather than a path, acquisition verifies the locked inode is still the file at the lock path and retries otherwise. attrs.problem: The JSONL backend's write-handle claim excluded a second writer only inside one backend instance. The seam needed durable cross-process write ownership whose arbiter lives outside every writer process, because no writer outlives every failure mode.

name: 2026-09-13-liveshare-protocol-and-owner-surfaces

An owner creates a share for one session from DSH itself. The share is published to the Liveshare server, a service both sides can reach, and DSH returns a link. Opening that link shows the session rendered by the owner's own DSH with its own plugins, so the reader never needs the owner's configuration. The reader's list contains the source Session and any children that reader created through the share. Workspace names, membership, and ordering are trimmed to those Sessions; unrelated Sessions and workspaces stay hidden.

Sending the session log is not the same thing: the colleague would need your plugins, configuration, and sandbox to render it, and the session only makes sense while it is running on your machine.

name: 2026-09-14-unattended-browser-terminal-reclamation

attrs.decision:
A browser terminal is reclaimed only after no window holds it and the Host continuously confirms idle activity for two hours. Running work and unknown activity cancel the idle deadline. When work finishes, a fresh full grace period starts; command runtime and output silence never impose a deadline. Explicit tab close and Session or Host disposal retain their authority to terminate work.

| Situation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| A connected window holds the tab, including a collapsed sidebar or inactive Session | Retain the terminal. |
| One of several holding windows disappears | Retain while another window holds it. |
| The final window disappears while a command is running, stopped, waiting for input, or running in the background | Preserve the work, regardless of runtime. |
| No window holds a positively confirmed idle terminal | Start the full grace period and recheck before cleanup. |
| A window returns before cleanup | Reattach the same process and cancel reclamation. |
| The saved process is gone | Preserve the tab and show localized unavailability with a New terminal action. Only an explicit click replaces it in place with a fresh identity. |

name: 2026-09-20-spawn-agent-preset-selection
title: Independent spawn preset selection and restoration

attrs.decision:
An explicit spawn preset id resolves the currently registered definition, even when it equals the parent's id. Omission joins the parent's exact live revision. Selecting a named configuration accepts its current declaration and resolution failures; inheriting an active composition preserves its plugin instances even after that declaration changes or is removed.

An independently selected child records the existing `agent-preset/selected` event before its first own `subagent/descriptor`. Cold restoration excludes the inherited fork prefix and uses that ordering to identify independent selection, then reads the selected id from the existing `agentPreset` projection. A missing projection rejects restoration rather than silently switching to the parent's composition.

Historical children without this ordering retain the implicit join. A creation header can contain an inherited preset id, while a fork's seed can contain an ancestor's selection and an old child can record a selection after its descriptor. None of these facts establishes independent selection at child creation. The ordering marker preserves those histories without adding a descriptor field or another event type.
attrs.problem: Spawned agents need reusable combinations of persona, tools, and skills without replacing the [implicit parent-preset join](../../archived/bug-fix/2026-08-10-child-agents-join-their-parent-preset.md). Restoration must distinguish an independent selection from historical child logs without changing the Session format or fork behavior.

name: 2026-10-14-host-release-change-refresh-prompt
title: Prompt to reload when the Host release changes instead of hot-replacing across releases

attrs.decision:
A release is the Host's version identity: a version plus an optional source commit. The name deliberately differs from "build", which names the build process and its artifacts.

The change touches three owners: client-modules (producing, publishing, and comparing the release identity), the shared client build preset (fixing the commit into the Host artifact), and ui-settings-general (the confirmation dialog). web-app and client-hmr are unchanged.

### Behavior

A page applies Host graphs and rebuilt frames only while the connected Host serves the release the page booted from. Every module the page runs therefore belongs to its boot release: either the boot artifacts unchanged, or the boot artifacts plus hot replacements published by a Host of that same release.

| The Host serves another release (version or commit differs) | Nothing from it is applied, rebuilt frames are ignored, and a dialog shows the Host's...
attrs.problem:
After `dsh web` is upgraded, or after a developer restarts `pnpm run dev:web` at another commit, an open browser page reconnects to the new Host automatically while its static shell stays at the old release. name: 2026-10-15-deepseek-search-fetch-api
title: Direct DeepSeek Search and Fetch APIs

The [web-deepseek-api plugin](../../../../packages/web/web-deepseek-api/README.md) implements it behind the existing `web_search` and `web_fetch` tools. ### Protocol selection and deployment

The APIs register as `deepseek-search-api` and `deepseek-fetch-api`. Messages search remains separately registered as `deepseek-official`. The web service selects each provider through `web.searchProvider` and `web.fetchProvider`, which the Search and Fetch menus on the Web search and fetch page set independently; the shipped composition selects local HTTP fetch and no search provider, which runs the Search API outside the DeepSeek model routes, as the [selection decision](../architecture/2026-10-29-web-prov...

The reviewer assigns user-sourced text the `user-instruction` role, including existing history and tasks admitted before Auto was selected. The user may be a human or a supervising caller. Both can define the task and authorize an exact medium-risk action, target, and scope. The current child's creation prompt and direct-parent messages keep their subordinate role; inherited and unverified creation prompts remain facts. name: 2026-10-19-sdk-native-user-questions
title: SDK native user questions

attrs.decision:
The TypeScript and Python clients accept a question callback and advertise it during initialization. The SDK server adapts the existing user-questions seam to a bidirectional RPC only for its exact owned root Agents. Clients without the capability keep native in-process answerers. Tool definitions and the service's live-root and delegation checks remain shared with the desktop composition.

Question identity is independent of the JSON-RPC envelope so cancellation can identify outstanding host work. The runtime validates a complete answer batch, aborts pending requests when the tool or server stops, and ignores late responses. The host owns answer collection; the SDK neither chooses answers nor treats missing input as approval. The [protocol reference](../../../../packages/sdk/protocol/README.md#native-user-questions) owns wire details.

name: 2026-10-26-manual-generation-continuation
title: Manual generation continuation

attrs.decision:
The play action submits `content: []` through the existing Session prompt API. The API assigns `source.kind: 'retry'`; unchanged AgentLoop admission records an empty `user/message` and opens a normally balanced new turn. Chat presents a compact continuation-request receipt while the log retains the empty input. The original failed turn remains closed.

The Session API owns the fixed-size `conversationContinuation` projection and shares its value with the browser. Admission requires an eligible failure, true idle ownership, and no pending human input. An appended empty retry message admits the new turn, preserving eligibility if its request also fails.

The six-code manual allowlist stays independent of provider retry policy. Non-waking injected context accompanies the request. The accepted user message retains request-id deduplication after the inbox input is claimed. Reusing ordinary message admission avoids a Loop branch and a separate durable acceptance event.
attrs.problem: Users need another request after a model failure without inserting an artificial instruction. Browser paging can omit the failed turn's start, and streaming must not repeatedly copy history.

name: 2026-11-02-liveshare-plugin-method-catalog
title: LiveShare plugin method catalog

attrs.decision:
The catalog is enumerated from the Typert local registry at runtime. One entry is emitted per bundle, using the bundle's localized title when available and the component package title otherwise. Endpoint descriptions come from the registered Remote descriptors. A share stores only method-level policies: the Host intersects each policy with the catalog before the Gateway dispatches a call.

The catalog excludes the DSH core bundles. Their methods remain governed by the existing Session and Workspace sharing roles, not by plugin permissions. The core bundle names are derived from `PROFILE_TEMPLATES`, so the exclusion follows the shipped profile composition instead of a second hand-maintained list. LiveShare's own bundle is excluded because it is the sharing implementation, not a capability a share can grant itself.
attrs.problem: LiveShare used to expose plugin endpoints through a declaration API. The API let a plugin name arbitrary endpoints, so a catalog mistake could widen a viewer's reach without a corresponding Gateway check. The replacement needs one source of truth that says which plugin methods a share may expose.

The browser keeps what the code host does not hold: the review summary and decision until submission, the records of Agent references and published comments, and the outgoing direct write whose outcome needs confirmation. Comments on local changes never had a host destination; they go to the main input as before. Comment drafts an earlier panel kept in the browser stay readable: they show beside their code as browser drafts, can move into the pending review, and keep Submit review disabled while a pending review exists; without one, Submit review publishes them as one review as before.

name: 2026-11-17-live-subagent-model-selection-setting
title: Live subagent model-selection setting

attrs.decision:
`SubagentModelSelectionConfig.allowedRoutes()` reads the volatile `enabled` value at each call and returns `undefined` immediately when selection is disabled; otherwise it validates `allowedModels` and returns a detached route list. The `subagent` executor and `list_subagent_models` call it through `ctx.get('subagentModelSelection')` for explicit route selection by model-selectable tools and for every discovery call, so an edit applies to the next call in every running, restored, and child Session. Operational labels may coexist without satisfying either dimension.

### Kinds

The kind set is closed and mutually exclusive:

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind/feature` | Adds or intentionally changes behavior. |
| `kind/bug-fix` | Corrects incorrect behavior. |
| `kind/doc` | Makes documentation the dominant intent. |
| `kind/testing` | Changes tests or testing infrastructure without changing product behavior. |
| `kind/cleanup` | Preserves behavior while maintaining or simplifying implementation or repository process. |
| `kind/dependency` | Updates dependencies without another dominant intent. |

[`verify-default-product-isolation`](../../../../scripts/verify-default-product-isolation.ts) runs in static CI and package hygiene. It follows runtime dependencies, optional dependencies, and peers from every app and the Python runtime, resolves workspace and npm aliases, and identifies experimental packages by their npm prefix or repository directory. Publication denylist membership has no effect on this classification. The bundles the launcher names in `OPTIONAL_BUNDLES` are the one declared exception ([shipped optional bundles](2026-09-15-shipped-optional-bundles.md)).

The source check also reads runtime imports in the selected packages, installation-owned profile bundle lists, bundle patches, shipped agent presets, and declared configuration trees. It loads the default Web layers with the production patch parser and composes them with the same patch engine used at boot. The effective rows and patched Include trees are checked, so an id-only patch cannot hide a replacement group's plugins. Disabled plugin rows remain checked; ordinary plugin configuration data is not interpreted as another Loader entry list. Missing default roots fail the check.

The default Web source graph s...
attrs.problem: Public npm availability does not make an experimental package part of the default product. Direct manifest checks miss dependency aliases, transitive installation paths, runtime imports declared only for development, and plugins loaded by configuration. The release smoke installs every tarball together, so the presence of experimental packages in its consumer directory does not identify what the default product requires.

name: 2026-09-14-generated-cli-help-reference
title: Generate the CLI reference from command help

attrs.decision:
The CLI reference captures the supported `dsh` launcher's help, the plugin forwarder's help, and each shipped profile's help, then recursively discovers the subcommands listed in each page's `Commands:` section. Shipped profile names come from `PROFILE_TEMPLATES`. Every page retains its complete help text; identical alias help appears once with all invocation forms.

Generation uses temporary Harness and Agents homes. Help exits before application work starts and requires no server or model. The plugin forwarder exposes its own help before pnpm arguments; flags after the pnpm command remain pnpm input.

The generated bilingual pages retain CLI output in its original language. `verify-cli-help` compares the complete pages and pairing record and runs with the documentation checks.
attrs.problem: Launcher flags, profile options, and nested commands have separate owners. A manually maintained command reference can omit subcommands or retain obsolete defaults.

name: 2026-09-15-shipped-optional-bundles
title: Ship optional bundles with the installation

attrs.decision:
The launcher names in `OPTIONAL_BUNDLES` (`packages/util/official-bundles/src/bundles.ts`, beside the profile templates) the bundles the installation ships for a person to switch on. Each must be a runtime dependency of `apps/cli` that declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and no shipped profile template selects it. The plugin manager's `listBundles` reports such a bundle as `optional`: switched off until selected, never removable, resolved from the installation like any installation-supplied bundle. The Web plugin page presents offered optional bundles in its Official group, tagged experimental when the package is experimental, ahead of the profile's own installed bundles.

Default-product isolation keeps its rules with one declared exception: an optional bundle's dependency graph is outside the default product. The static gate skips the `dependencies` edge from `@deepseek-ai/dsh` to a listed bundle and still rejects a runtime import, a shipped composition, a preset, or a default template that names it, an experimental dependency the list does not name, and a listed name that is not a runtime dependency or not a bundle. The workspace-constraints check accepts the same `dependencies` edges ...
attrs.problem: The Web plugin page manages only the bundles a person installed into the profile. An official experimental layer such as Agent Teams had to be found on npm and installed by name before it could be switched on, and [default-product isolation](2026-09-12-default-product-experimental-isolation.md) kept every experimental package out of the installation's runtime dependencies, so nothing shipped with dsh could offer it.

name: 2026-09-17-persistence-schema-review
title: Persistence schema policy and review

attrs.decision:
Inventory format 2 records supported compatibility metadata with the affected property. The metadata names its binding, policy version, literal discriminator, unknown-kind preservation promise, and qualified attribution kinds. Policy-bearing graphs use a separate fingerprint domain; graphs without a bound policy retain format-1 normalization and fingerprints. Inventory versions describe schema tooling, independently of Session format versions.

The extractor accepts explicit source bindings only at the core-owned source declaration and requires a literal user or developer role at each use. Producer annotations qualify complete wire-kind groups. The classifier permits a qualified new attribution kind only when both saved schemas carry matching promises. Existing kinds remain subject to structural comparison; removals, retroactive qualification, reserved identities, and unrelated breaking changes retain strict classification. Runtime owners establish and test the promised preservation behavior before activating a binding.

An optional property with no JSON value is normally omitted from the extracted graph. `@persistenceReserved` explicitly retains such a property as optional `never`...
attrs.problem: Structural fingerprints identify changed persistence types, but a fingerprint alone cannot explain a shared change or distinguish a declared reader promise from an assumption about runtime behavior. Names derived from union positions and traversal paths also change when unrelated siblings are added, obscuring the fields a reviewer needs to inspect.

name: 2026-09-17-windows-runtime-signature-cache
title: Windows runtime signature cache

attrs.decision:
Cache complete signed runtime files by original content, public certificate, SignTool bytes, signing-script bytes and cache format. Keep valid vendor signatures. Restore a cache hit through a private staged copy only after checking the input record, signed-file digest, Windows trust, timestamp and configured certificate; reject invalid entries without automatic repair or hardware fallback. Publish complete entries atomically, and retain an existing valid entry when concurrent publishers collide.

Share the cache only within the current Windows account. Require a fixed local drive, current-account ownership and a private destination DACL; reject linked or redirected paths. Programs running as that account remain trusted. Explicit migration copies complete integrity-checked entries without modifying its source or replacing an existing valid entry. Different timestamp bytes at the same input/policy key do not require replacement; every actual restoration still verifies Windows trust.

The default cache lives beside the account's existing signing state under the user profile. AppData is unsuitable for this default because an MSIX launcher can redirect new files into its private package...
attrs.problem: Windows packaging reconstructs unsigned native dependencies on each build. Signing unchanged Python and LibreOffice files repeats hardware-token and timestamp operations. Starting PowerShell for each public-key inspection also repeats process initialization.

name: 2026-09-17-windows-signature-completion
title: Separate Windows hardware signing from timestamp completion

attrs.decision:
Sign a private PE copy once without a timestamp. Release the hardware interlock only after successful execution and Windows verification of the configured primary signature. Hardware or primary-verification failures retain the interlock; no path automatically recovers it. Appended signatures are unsupported.

Timestamp fresh copies of the frozen signed file without signing credentials. Only normal failure or warning exits permit another attempt: at most three calls, with one- and two-second delays. Launch failures, uncertain termination, storage changes and verification failures stop immediately. The preflight's overall 60-second deadline includes these operations and does not guarantee three full subprocess deadlines.

Require Windows trust, timestamp and certificate identity. Remove unsigned signature attributes from private copies with the configured SignTool and compare their complete normalized bytes. A removal warning is accepted only when all bytes remain unchanged. Certificate equality alone cannot exclude different content signed by the same certificate; full-file equality avoids a custom PE or ASN.1 canonicalizer.

SignTool uses short filenames with the original extension...
attrs.problem: A combined SignTool command reports timestamp failure as signing failure. Retrying it repeats hardware access, while treating every timestamp error as an uncertain private-key outcome requires administrator recovery. Public timestamp-only requests can fail independently of the token.

name: 2026-09-19-no-unknown-casts
title: Prohibit new assertions to unknown

attrs.decision:
New direct assertions to `unknown` are prohibited in first-party JavaScript and TypeScript, including tests, fixtures, benchmarks, and scripts. Both `as unknown` and `<unknown>` syntax are covered, including parenthesized target types and union targets with a direct `unknown` member. An `unknown` declaration remains valid: external data can enter as `const value: unknown = JSON.parse(text)` and reach its declared parser before use. Typed in-process values retain the existing rule against unnecessary runtime validation.

The [checker](../../../../scripts/verify-no-unknown-casts.ts), exposed as `pnpm run verify-no-unknown-casts`, uses the TypeScript syntax tree. It scans tracked source files and non-ignored untracked source files; vendored sources and frozen archived Agent Notes retain their ownership exclusions. The checker ignores comments, strings, and declarations of `unknown`.

Existing assertions have an exact baseline keyed by repository-relative path, a SHA-256 digest of the assertion's syntax tokens, and occurrence count. Baseline edits may only delete entries or decrease counts; reviewers must reject added files, new fingerprints, and increased counts. New or changed assert...
attrs.problem:
An assertion through `unknown` removes TypeScript's compatibility check between the original value and a subsequent asserted type. Production code can hide an incorrect interface, and tests can claim that an incomplete fixture satisfies a service. Existing uses also include legitimate widening of untyped parser results, which can use explicit `unknown` declarations instead.

The repository contains assertions across many independent package and test owners. Removing all of them in one change wou...

name: 2026-09-21-reject-silent-empty-catch
title: Reject silent empty catch clauses

attrs.decision:
The [checker](../../../../scripts/verify-empty-catch.ts), exposed as `pnpm run verify-empty-catch`, parses first-party JavaScript and TypeScript with the TypeScript syntax tree and reports an empty clause, one whose body holds no statement other than `;`, that is unnamed, unexplained, or wraps a multi-statement `try`. A bare `_` counts as unnamed; lint requires an unused binding to start with `_`, so a conforming name such as `_alreadyGone` states the expected failure. A clause body with any other statement is out of scope because syntax cannot show whether it handles the error. The checker establishes the form; review establishes that the name and the reason are true, using the guidance in [dsh-error-handling](../../../skills/dsh-error-handling/SKILL.md#empty-catch-clauses).

Existing clauses have an exact baseline keyed by repository-relative path, a SHA-256 digest of the clause's syntax tokens together with its broken conditions, and occurrence count. Including the broken conditions makes turning a recorded one-statement `try` into a wider one, or deleting a recorded reason, a new finding, while edits inside the `try` that keep its conditions keep the clause's identity. The base...
attrs.problem: An empty `catch` discards every failure of its `try`, including defects the author did not expect. The root rule requires such a clause to name the error, state why discarding it is safe, and keep its `try` to one statement, so that the clause discards only the failure its author considered. Without a check, new clauses drifted from the rule, and existing clauses broke it across many unrelated package and test owners.

name: 2026-09-28-dual-release-install-layout-work-budget
title: Dual-release install layout work budget

attrs.decision:
`scripts/verify-npm-install-layout.ts` decides growth with `assertResolutionWorkBudget`, which bounds `dshPackagesPerVersion * checkedDshEdges` against `MAX_RESOLUTION_WORK_UNITS = 1_134_400`. Both counts come from the summary `assertDualDshInstallLayout` returns, so the budget applies to the graph npm actually produced rather than to a prediction of it. A graph above the budget fails with its own counts, the budget, and the instruction to measure the new resolution cost and raise the constant.

It is a hang guard, not the growth criterion: a runner up to four times slower than the measured host cannot decide the gate's outcome, and deriving it from the budget keeps the two values from drifting apart.

name: 2026-10-05-product-package-classification
title: Require product use or an explicit package classification

attrs.decision:
Nonexperimental packages have effective product use or an explicit entry in the [package policy](../../../../scripts/product-package-policy.ts).
