name: 2026-10-08-session-reader-compatibility-review
title: Session versions follow reader compatibility

attrs.decision:
The user chose reader behavior as the version criterion. A same-version change is permitted when older readers either resume correctly, safely ignore optional features while preserving their records, or refuse required features before execution, mutation, or tail repair. Feature absence must preserve existing behavior. Required-feature refusal needs an upgrade diagnostic; already released binaries retain their existing diagnostics, so review identifies any limitation explicitly.

New readers preserve the meaning of supported historical records and accept valid mixtures of old and new representations within one Session. Removing a required field or changing its representation is not automatically a bump: the replacement must remain distinguishable, and released-reader behavior must satisfy the same admission requirements. A version increase is required when no effective existing discriminator prevents unsafe interpretation. Reusing a logged value with a different meaning is one example; missing admission checks are another.

The schema classifier identifies structural changes requiring compatibility review instead of declaring them inherently version-breaking. Every schema differenc...

An optional environment header field illustrates the cost: sessions that omit the feature can retain identical logs, while sessions that require it can be refused by older readers. A global bump also excludes feature-free sessions and requires a new generation and adjacent migration. Conversely, an unknown field or value does not establish safe refusal: permissive readers can ignore required meaning, an...

name: 2026-10-15-node-24-runtime-floor
title: Node runtime floor and compatibility coverage

attrs.decision:
Set `engines.node` to `>=24.9.0`. Node 24.9 is the minimum for DSH and its development carriers, including the experimental OAR subagent integration, whose `@botiverse/oar` library requires Node 24. This supersedes the [Node 22.19 floor](../../archived/process/2026-07-06-node-engine-floor.md); its Node 23 exclusion remains satisfied, and the declaration policy below remains narrower than the runtime floor. Migration instructions live in the [upgrade guide](../../../../docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-rc.2/node-24/guide.md).

The primary Node 24 jobs own complete typechecking and unit coverage. Focused compatibility jobs run on pinned Node 24.9 and Node 26. Node 24.9 supports the existing `import.meta.main` script entrypoints and native TypeScript stripping. Pinning 24.9 exercises this verified minimum and its v1 private module loader; the primary jobs track the latest Node 24 and exercise its v2 loader, introduced in 24.12.0. A floating `24` compatibility job would duplicate the primary loader coverage and stop testing the minimum.

The Node 24.9 compatibility job also builds artifacts and checks that the shipped Web CLI starts and disposes with full-text Session search disabled. Command-...
attrs.problem: The root `engines.node` range promises that the installed workspace supports each admitted runtime. Its minimum must cover both the runtime APIs DSH uses and the declared requirements of installed dependencies. Otherwise strict installation can reject a supported version before DSH starts.

name: 2026-10-18-source-first-metadata-builds
title: Generate metadata before package compilation

attrs.decision:
Artifact and declaration-only builds run source-only Typert generation before package compilation. The existing generator rejects workspace build outputs and unresolved workspace imports, so a metadata producer cannot depend on its own generated declarations through another source package. TypeScript retains compiler-face ownership and rejects project-reference cycles. Generation failure stops dependent compilation and bundling.

The root bundler uses `decoratorPlugin()` to lower standard TypeScript decorators without generating metadata again. The public `typertPlugin()` retains package/workspace generation and its Worker Thread behavior. [Development](../../../../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout) owns the current command order.

This ordering replaces only the generation placement in [local gate speed-ups](2026-10-12-local-gate-speedups.md), [lossless build speed-ups](2026-10-11-lossless-build-speedups.md), [the build/check split](2026-10-11-build-artifacts-check-split.md), and [Remote method generation](../architecture/2026-08-02-typert-remote-method-calls.md). Their other optimizations, failure guarantees, public plugin behavior, and historical measurements remain ...
attrs.problem: A Host package can consume generated Remote declarations without becoming a Client package. Generating metadata during Host bundling forces the build to identify those consumers, delay their compilation, and propagate that delay to their callers. TypeScript project references already describe the package dependencies; maintaining another source-import graph duplicates ordering work.

name: 2026-10-20-weighted-approval-status-gate-with-check-run-label
title: Weighted approval keeps its commit status gate and publishes the decision label from an App

attrs.decision:
The publisher keeps writing the `weighted approval` commit status exactly as before: `pending` while the policy is unmet, `success` when it holds, and `error` when setup or evaluation fails. Branch rules keep requiring that status. That behavior, including keeping an unmet policy `pending`, is what the [archived decision](../../archived/process/2026-09-09-blocked-weighted-approvals-remain-pending.md) records; this change adds the label beside it instead of changing the gate.

name: 2026-11-04-plugin-entry-value-exports
title: Plugin entries must not add value exports

attrs.decision:
The gate [verify-plugin-entry-exports](../../../../scripts/verify-plugin-entry-exports.ts) enforces the rule for both plugin forms:

- **Scope**: every `packages/<group>/<package>/src/index.ts` that is a plugin entry. An entry that exports a value named `apply` is a function plugin. An entry without `apply` whose default export is a class the Loader can construct is a service plugin. Libraries, a default export that is not a class, and an abstract default class are not checked; an abstract class defines a capability seam that providers extend, and the Loader cannot construct it.
- **Compiler faces**: the gate reads each entry through the Host compiler face and then the Client face, and the first face that compiles an entry classifies it. An entry that neither face compiles fails the gate, and so does a corpus without a function plugin entry or without a service plugin entry.
- **Rule**: a function plugin entry may export `name`, `inject`, `Config`, and `apply`, and a service plugin entry may export its default class under any name. Either may also export types and values whose every construct signature builds an instance whose base types reach Cordis `Service` or the global `Error`...

name: 2026-11-13-no-new-cordis-root-reads

name: 2026-06-20-unify-agent-and-session-id
title: Unify the agent id and the session id

attrs.decision:
An agent's registry id equals its session id. `CreateAgentOptions` accepts one `sessionId` used for both final registry entries; resume registers the agent under `resumeSessionId`; in-process subagent creation uses the child session id; and `Session.id` derives from `header.id`. A remote ACP run has no local agent/session pair: it keeps one parent-minted lifecycle id while the child server's wire-local session id remains private to ACP calls. The existing creation transaction, final-entry collision checks, and exact-entry detach semantics remain; maps and fields whose sole job was translating between local ids are gone.

The config-driven path keeps `agents[].id` as a stable configuration label, not a live routing identity. An ordinary fresh start mints the combined id `${label}-session-${randomUUID()}` so durable restarts do not collide. A coupled app may pre-mint and pass an exact `sessionId`: first use creates it, while an AgentLoop remount with an already-present persistence service resumes materialized history under that same identity. `resumeSessionId` instead requires an existing persisted identity. The two exact-id inputs are mutually exclusive. Stdio uses the resume-or-cre...

name: 2026-07-17-one-send-one-turn
title: Remove implicit batching from ordinary sends

attrs.decision:
Each successful `send()` creates one independent FIFO queue item. If that item runs, it is the only ordinary message in its turn. An item can be dropped before it starts, so the precise guarantee is at most one turn rather than exactly one; two sends are never silently combined.

Before inserting a message, `send()` checks the agent state and accepts an already identified, deeply frozen value. The durable splice and `agent/inbox/inserted { message }` retain its `MessageId`; the pending message remains addressable through `Inbox.replace()` and `Inbox.remove()` until the driver claims or discards it. The [claimed pre-step inbox reference](../../../../packages/core/agent-loop/README.md) owns the current lifecycle.

If messages A and B are both processed, B's turn starts only after A records `turn/end` and A's durability checkpoint settles. B's request therefore sees whatever closed result A left in the same session log. A checkpoint error is reported, but settlement only releases this ordering barrier; it does not make a failed write durable. Broad `cancel()`, disposal, or a failure before `turn/start` can instead discard an unstarted item without opening an empty turn.

At a turn bou...
attrs.problem:
Suppose a caller submits message A and then message B with two `Agent.send()` calls. Implicit batching can put A and B in one turn simply because both are waiting when the driver reads its queue. The caller made two calls, but the loop silently turns them into one unit of work.

That grouping depends on timing rather than caller intent. Calls from one synchronous stack, neighboring microtasks, event listeners, and model callbacks could be grouped differently even though every caller used the sam...

name: 2026-07-23-acp-automation-only-protocol
title: ACP as an automation-only protocol

attrs.decision:
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp` is an automation transport under [`packages/acp/acp`](../../../../packages/acp/acp/README.md), outside the `ui` package group. Its public protocol contains standard automation controls rather than presentation: persistent session creation/list/resume/close, one in-flight prompt per session, model configuration, stdio/HTTP MCP mounting, committed semantic updates, cancellation, concurrent sessions, and one-shot permission requests. Prompts preserve text and supported raster images in wire order, while resource links flatten to bracketed textual references; the bridge still rejects additional directories, audio, embedded resources, malformed or empty prompts, unknown sessions, and overlapping prompts.

Image capability is truthful rather than structural: `initialize` advertises it only when a durable attachment store exists and the configured exact provider/model resolves with explicit image input. Each prompt snapshots its exact route before asynchronous admission, strictly decodes every image block, and delegates the complete batch to `AttachmentStore.saveImages()` before publishing the user event. That same snapshot drives the admitted turn even if the next-...
attrs.problem:
The ACP bridge had become a second interactive product UI. It translated durable events into editor cards, terminal metadata, diffs, plans, titles, reasoning, commands, modes, model and permission pickers, session navigation, and human elicitation. Those responsibilities duplicated the TUI and the Web client while coupling an automation transport to UI services, persistence queries, presentation policy, and editor-specific conventions.

ACP still has one useful role: another agent or automated c...

name: 2026-07-28-remove-synthetic-log-only-turns
title: Remove synthetic turns for log-only events

attrs.decision:
`SessionStore.appendOutOfBand()`, `OutOfBandSessionEventMap`, and `OutOfBandSessionEventType` do not exist. A plugin that owns a log-only event appends it through `Session`; when the operation promises durability, it explicitly awaits `ctx.sessions.flush(session)`. No turn is opened solely to obtain that checkpoint.

Core permits merge-extensible events between turns because only their declaring plugin knows whether they are execution-scoped or standalone.

The title service appends `session/title` directly after its existing service, revision, cancellation, and live-session checks. The bundled model helper appends its literal `session/title-llm-request` record before dispatch. Persistence admits both through the bounded `session/event` path and drains them at ordinary checkpoints and lifecycle teardown; neither append forces a flush merely because it is between turns. A fallback, auxiliary request record, or accepted provider title may therefore appear after `turn/end` and before the next `turn/start`. Manual compaction uses the same between-turn capability for a `compaction/* { turn: null }` bracket, but explicitly flushes the closed attempt because `/compact` promises durability...
attrs.problem:
The session store exposed `appendOutOfBand()` so a plugin could publish a late log-only event while no agent turn was running. The method wrapped that event in `turn/start` and `turn/end`, then flushed it. This preserved the old rule that every durable event had to live inside a turn, but it made one identifier mean both a model-loop execution and a persistence-only update.

That rule was introduced when persistence recovery treated the last `turn/end` as the only committed boundary. The persist...

name: 2026-08-09-explicit-schedule-time-zone
title: Explicit Schedule time-zone boundary

attrs.decision:
The browser zone is request-local source data. The Web client samples `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` for every prompt. The Host accepts an optional `clientTimeZone`, validates and canonicalizes `UTC` or an IANA Area/Location at the RPC boundary, and logs it on that exact `user-rpc` message. Invalid values reject prompt admission. Non-browser clients may omit it.

Time-context derives unique, mixed, or missing browser facts from original user-rpc messages in the open turn. A unique zone formats the clock and tells the model to interpret otherwise-unqualified dates and times in that zone. Mixed or missing browser-zone records tell the model to ask the user. The configured or process zone is only a display fallback and is never presented as user authority.

Schedule accepts no implicit local zone. `at` is either a strict offset-bearing RFC 3339 string or exact `{ date, time, time_zone }`. The structured form requires its zone even when time-context just showed the model a browser zone. Schedule does not import time-context, inspect user-message sources, read a Session header, or produce a confirmation error. Its parser validates the explicit value, rejects daylight...

Implicit local `at` input made a browser fact into shared product state. Travel, concurrent tabs, missing browser-zone records, and old Sessions then needed a confirmation protocol merely to decide whether an omitted field was safe.

name: 2026-08-30-jsonl-only-session-persistence

name: 2026-09-09-nontransactional-loader
title: Keep Loader mutations non-transactional

attrs.decision:
Revert the five commits in #932, resolving package moves and retaining independent later behavior. The reported merge commit belongs to the larger #936 dependency chain; reverting its first-parent diff would remove unrelated repository-plugin support. The [vendor ledger](../../../../vendor/README.md#local-modifications) records every retained source change against the unchanged pins.

Loader changes entry options eagerly. EntryGroup starts siblings concurrently and logs application failures; EntryTree waits for outstanding work without rejecting failed fibers. Neither restores a previous plugin or configuration. Include keeps the running tree after an invalid file, but plugin failures can leave a partially applied tree.

Application consumers own their completion checks. The CLI waits for its fallback HMR service before installing live patch watchers. The directory chooser checks the entries it mounts. The chooser and browser package runner capture the first fiber-disposal result before removing the entry, then await it before reporting teardown complete. Preset mounting waits for its subtree and reports import, activation, and missing-service failures. [App boot](../../../../packa...

These changes make the vendored implementation substantially different from its pinned sources. Application startup and profile patch watching also depend on that settlement implicitly.

name: 2026-09-11-remove-e2b-providers
title: Remove the E2B execution providers

attrs.decision:
The repository excludes the E2B sandbox owner, filesystem provider and subprocess provider, their SDK dependency, integration fixtures, opt-in workflow and generated registrations. A local/remote metadata label adds no authority to those operations.

The E2B experiment supplied one remote filesystem/process world for file tools, Bash, PTY and language servers while the Harness, credentials, model transport and session state stayed on the host. name: 2026-09-17-unified-subagent-activations
title: Unified subagent activations

attrs.decision:
`startActivation()` is the consumer entry point for every provider. A published handle exposes child identity, a result promise, and disposal of that exact activation. The caller signal cancels unpublished creation only. Local results wait for pending input and owned descendants before closing admission, so descendant replies can contribute to the final answer. Both local and external result promises settle after cleanup and notifications. Parent waits use that same completion promise; a captured execution result survives cleanup failure, which disposal reports separately. Workflow consumers already wait for cleanup before continuing, so activation ownership needs no independent result-readiness and release signals.

Local spawn and fork providers contribute only `prepareContinuable()` data; the subagent service owns Agent creation and residency. The standalone in-process driver package is removed. Structured tools, validation, instructions, and terminal guards attach to one activation and close with it. After capture, that activation rejects further input; cold resume reconstructs an ordinary conversation without the previous schema.

ACP, DSH SDK, Codex, and Claude Code retain th...
attrs.problem: Local one-shot execution and continuable residency separately owned child creation, cancellation, structured capture, results, and cleanup. Foreground and Job-backed tool paths added more ownership paths. Workflow code still needed to await a result, while external backends needed one process execution without acquiring a multi-turn protocol.

name: 2026-09-19-remove-desktop-profile-core-cleanup
title: Remove the Desktop production profile core-package cleanup

Delete `apps/desktop/src/profile-core-cleanup.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/profile-packages.ts`, and their two specs. `DesktopProjectManager.applyRelease` validates the runtime descriptor, migrates profile settings, creates the profile files, and removes the projections a link-backend launch wrote through the shared `removeLinkProjections`; beyond that, neither production nor development launches modify the profile's `node_modules`, manifest, overrides, lockfile, or `desktop-runtime-state.json`.

It targeted two kinds of residue: earlier Desktop builds had ins...

name: 2026-10-05-native-or-ptc-presentation
title: One tool invocation form per agent

attrs.decision: Each agent selects `native` or `ptc`. Native presentation exposes visible capability schemas. PTC presentation exposes only `run_code` and the generated SDK. The registry rejects `both` in configuration. Presets can select different supported modes in one application.
attrs.problem: Mixed tool presentation carries direct function schemas and a program SDK for the same capabilities. It adds schema-ordering, admission, configuration, and test combinations without a separate execution capability. The [PTC decision](../feature/2026-06-15-ptc.md) still owns the registry, runtime, and nested-call rules.

name: 2026-10-09-preset-owned-subagent-composition
title: Preset-owned subagent composition

attrs.decision:
New subagent requests select an Agent Preset where the provider supports it. Persona and tools come from its plugin list. Fork inherits the parent's preset revision; model and effort selection keep their existing configuration. No preset-level filter or finer plugin split is added without a concrete consumer.

`dsh-tool-subagent` rejects removed `persona` and `toolFilter` keys at load, including empty values, because deleting Schemastery fields alone does not reject unknown configuration. The [upgrade guide](../../../../docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.1/subagent-preset-composition/guide.md) states the lost independent override capability and the migration.

Released child descriptors keep their persona and filter fields, parsing, and cold-resume application. The [original composition note](../feature/2026-07-12-subagent-persona-tool-filter-and-depth.md) remains active for these historical semantics and the independent depth policy. The [spawn preset decision](../feature/2026-09-20-spawn-agent-preset-selection.md) continues to own selection and restoration identity.

The shipped child schedule deny lists are absent. Reminder schemas remain visible when inherited from the preset; eac...
attrs.problem: Agent Presets already compose persona and tool plugins. Independent child persona and tool-filter inputs create a second place to configure that composition. The shipped consumers of child filtering are the six schedule deny lists in the spawn and fork rows of the standard, PTC, and Cordis presets; reminder executors already refuse delegated callers.

name: 2026-10-13-text-derived-message-quotes
title: Recognize message quotes from Markdown text

attrs.decision:
Messages contain ordinary Markdown text. The shared blockquote matcher recognizes consecutive explicitly marked lines for UserText presentation. Hand-written and composer-created blockquotes have identical sent-message behavior. Quote previews display decoded text without running UserText rules over their contents. Session-reference and skill processing applies normally to quoted text; recognized Session labels retain the same presentation as the surrounding quote text.

The [rich-text quote feature](../feature/2026-08-26-web-rich-text-quotes.md) retains atomic draft nodes and semantic restoration spans. This decision supersedes only its durable quote-index distinction. UserText nodes and recognition ranges remain derived values.
attrs.problem: Quote-only content indexes duplicate information in Markdown text and require coordinated prompt, source, echo, and queue metadata. The same visible blockquote can acquire different presentation and direct-input behavior depending on how it was created.

name: 2026-10-29-inbox-only-agent-wait
title: Inbox-only Agent waits

attrs.decision:
`wait_agent` observes only its exact caller's next-step inbox through the existing insertion event. It subscribes before checking pending input, consumes nothing, and removes listeners and timers on input, timeout, cancellation, caller disposal, or tool unload. Queued next-turn input, other Agents' activity, and task-board changes do not end the wait.

Task commands append and flush their revisions without notifying waits or writing inbox messages. A caller sends an explicit message when a member needs to act on an update. No Agent method, shared waiting service, or task-specific waiting event is introduced.

This supersedes only the wait-signal decision in [Team task boards](../architecture/2026-10-19-team-task-board-inbox.md). Its tree authority, durable task storage, historical non-authority, and separation from ordinary controls remain applicable. No Session event generation changes.
attrs.problem: A task-board commit changes shared state but does not deliver input to a member. Ending every member's wait on each edit couples ordinary subagent controls to Team coordination and makes callers resume without a message explaining what needs attention.

name: 2026-10-29-team-task-only-projection
title: Team projection retains only tasks and mode

attrs.decision:
Project only tasks, saved mode, and their recovery metadata. Ignore `team/member` and `team/message/*` payloads without rebuilding or validating their former state machines. This deliberately gives up historical teammate and mailbox state recovery and the associated validation failures. The user accepted that loss; task recovery remains required.

Checkpoint version 7 invalidates prior state, including failures caused by retired records. The registry rebuilds from the unchanged Session log. Historical event declarations, format migrations, message sources, and attachment export remain supported; no Session format bump or log conversion is needed.

This partially supersedes the projection and mailbox-validation decisions in [Agent Teams](../feature/2026-08-05-agent-teams.md). The [subagent identity](../architecture/2026-10-15-agent-teams-as-subagents.md) and [inbox-only wait](2026-10-29-inbox-only-agent-wait.md) decisions remain active, as do task durability and shared-checkout semantics.
attrs.problem: The Team projection retained historical member, message, and delivery collections after subagent discovery and messaging replaced their runtime consumers. Its retired lifecycle and mailbox validators could still fail the current task board, while checkpoints retained message bodies with no current reader.

name: 2026-11-02-deepseek-deferred-tool-failures
title: Expose DeepSeek deferred-only request failures

attrs.decision:
The DeepSeek adapter sends deferred declarations unchanged and propagates provider rejection. This replaces the placeholder accommodation described by the [tool-update decision](../architecture/2026-09-20-dynamic-tool-updates.md), whose shared history projection remains authoritative.

Ordinary addition-only histories start with native tools or an empty set. Removals and first additions to an empty set rebuild native declarations; later deferred additions retain a native baseline. Explicit deferred-only registrations, direct adapter calls, and custom in-history routes can still produce all-deferred requests. Those configurations receive no adapter workaround.
attrs.problem: A synthetic immediate tool can make an all-deferred DeepSeek request acceptable while hiding an invalid tool-update projection. It also changes the request prefix and advertises a tool with no executor.

name: 2026-11-12-typescript-only-ptc
title: TypeScript-only PTC tool execution

attrs.decision:
`dsh-tool-executor-ptc` supports TypeScript only. It removes Python schema rendering and exports, language dispatch, completion presentation, and Python-specific binding exclusions. Unsupported providers fail during prompt assembly or execution through the selected executor, or when a private program tool is created. The PTC selection remains active so an invalid provider cannot expose inherited native tools. TypeScript programs retain their SDK, parameters, explicit output selection, canonical nested results and cancellation behavior.

The runtime service remains independent of tools. Its source-language descriptor lets each consumer check its own requirements; direct runtime and workflow consumers retain completion values. The Harness Python SDK, runtime wheels and other tools' Python environments have separate consumers and remain supported.

The [PTC foundation](../feature/2026-06-15-ptc.md) and [typed returns](../feature/2026-07-20-ptc-typed-tool-returns.md) remain active for their independent dispatch, durability and value semantics. Their language-specific facts follow this decision. The [archived language-dispatch decision](../../archived/feature/2026-07-31-ptc-language-dis...
attrs.problem: The Python tool SDK originally let a provider change the program language while retaining typed tool calls. Removing the experimental Python runtime left that presentation available to external providers, together with Python completion rendering and binding-name restrictions imposed on the Node provider. Shipped PTC compositions use TypeScript, so those paths maintain a second language without a repository-owned execution provider or profile replay.

name: 2026-06-19-real-api-e2e-ci
title: Real-API e2e in CI against the external DeepSeek API

attrs.decision:
A dedicated workflow, [.github/workflows/e2e.yml](../../../../.github/workflows/e2e.yml), separate from ci.yml, runs only `pnpm run test:e2e` against the external API using a repo secret, on trusted events, with a preflight that converts a missing secret into a loud failure instead of a false green. The keyless workflow remains separate so forkable quality gates and secret-consuming real-API gates keep different trigger and credential policies.

### A separate workflow, not a job in ci.yml

ci.yml's value is that it is keyless, forkable, and always-green: any contributor (including an outside fork) gets a complete keyless signal with no secret in the blast radius. Adding a secret-consuming job there would couple that always-green gate to credential availability and a different trigger policy. Keeping the secret-bearing work in its own file isolates the secret, trigger, and concurrency policy, and preserves ci.yml's property for forks. Different lifecycles → different files.

### Cost is not the constraint; reliability is

Internal inference cost is not the limiting constraint, so the workflow optimizes for coverage and signal. It runs every matching `*.e2e.ts` file on multiple trig...
attrs.problem: The harness leans hard on real-API tests by policy: [docs/testing.md](../../../../docs/testing.md) argues that a no-key suite proves the plumbing but not the product, and the [ACP inject postmortem](../../../../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md) is the standing proof — 178 keyless tests stayed green while a real ACP client session crashed instantly. The real-API e2e suite (`pnpm run test:e2e`, the `*.e2e.ts` files) exists precisely to close that gap: it drives the agent aga...

name: 2026-07-24-web-gui-browser-e2e-lane
title: Keyless browser e2e lane for the web GUI

attrs.decision:
`pnpm run test:web` carries a keyless, deterministic browser e2e lane under `apps/web/tests/`: recorded session-log fixtures replay through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-replay` against the real in-process web composition, with normalized aria goldens for user-visible states and in-process assertions for durable world state. Chromium runs the full lane; the [model and reasoning picker scenario](../../../../apps/web/tests/declared-reasoning.e2e.ts) also runs in WebKit to cover native mouse focus behavior. attrs.decision:
### Installed artifact boundary

The required Python runtime workflow builds the pure SDK wheel and each platform runtime wheel before behavior tests. Every native target installs those two local files into a new Python 3.10 virtual environment, changes to a temporary directory outside the repository, unsets `PYTHONPATH` and `DSH_RUNTIME_MODE`, and invokes only the public Python modules plus the packaged executable.

The black-box harness rejects a non-venv process, repository-relative working directory, source or editable import, unequal distribution versions, an SDK dependency that does not exactly pin the runtime version, an executable outside the installed runtime package, or an executable absent from the runtime distribution record. This installed-artifact identity check runs before the first agent request, so a behavior pass cannot conceal that the wrong code ran.

attrs.decision:
Status: proposed

English | [中文](2026-06-11-mutation-testing.zh.md)

## Problem

The per-file 100% coverage gate ([the quality-gates reference](../../../../docs/testing.md)) proves every line *executes* under test — not that any assertion would notice if the line were wrong. Under agent-written tests, coverage pressure can produce execution-without-assertion. Mutation testing measures what coverage cannot: whether the suite *kills* deliberately injected bugs.

## Proposal

Stryker (`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner`) over `packages/*/src`:

- **PR-scoped incremental runs** (changed files only) as a CI job — fast enough to gate merges once tuned.
- **Nightly full runs** with a tracked mutation score; start by recording, then set the threshold at the observed baseline and ratchet upward (same policy as coverage: thresholds only ever tighten).
- Surviving mutants are work items: an agent picks a survivor, writes the killing test, repeats — a well-shaped autonomous loop.
- Equivalent mutants (provably behavior-preserving) get annotated exclusions with reasons, mirroring the `/* v8 ignore */` policy.

Status: rejected — implementation (PR #679) falsified the parity premise: vitest's fake clock does not intercept `node:timers/promises`, so the swap costs deterministic fast tests for ~10 deleted lines

English | [中文](2026-07-26-builtin-timer-promises-for-hand-rolled-sleeps.zh.md)

## Problem

Three packages hand-roll promise-wrapped timers that the `node:timers/promises` builtin already provides, while other packages (`dsh-llm-mock-server` `pause()`, `dsh-lsp-stdio`, `dsh-acp-snapshot`) already use the builtin — so the hand-rolled copies are also a consistency gap:

- `packages/llm/llm-retry/src/index.ts` `cancellableDelay()` (~14 lines): `new Promise` + `setTimeout` + manual abort-listener add/remove, resolving `true` on elapse and `false` on abort, consumed once for the backoff wait.
- The former `workflow-worker-thread` host's `sleep()` (~7 lines, evaluated in PR #679): promise-wrapped unref'd `setTimeout` used as the dispose-grace bound.
- `packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/session.ts` `delay()` (~4 lines): bare promise-wrapped `setTimeout` used in polling/teardown waits.

## Proposal

name: 2026-07-26-dependency-swaps-rejected-by-nih-audit
title: Dependency swaps rejected by the 2026-07 NIH audit

attrs.decision:
Status: rejected — every swap below fails the net-simplification bar on evidence; recorded so the survey is not re-run from scratch

English | [中文](2026-07-26-dependency-swaps-rejected-by-nih-audit.zh.md)

## Problem

A repository-wide "Not Invented Here" audit (2026-07-26, ten parallel surveys covering every package group, scripts/, native/, vendor/ edges, python/, test infrastructure, and CI) asked of each hand-rolled surface: would a maintained external package or Node builtin delete it with a net win under the [dependency policy](../../implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)? The positive findings became their own proposed notes. The negative verdicts carry equal value — each names a plausible-looking swap whose hand-rolled shape is load-bearing — but would otherwise live only in a PR body. This note freezes them.
